# Read the SCF application and operate its retained grant purchase

Open the original public purchase as an operating reviewer workspace. Review its
source and terms, read both complete native results, export a closed Buyer view,
and receive that packet under another operator's private workspace.

This workflow uses the retained purchase. The original transaction, quote
identities, seller outcomes and source documents remain part of that packet.
Opening, reading, exporting and receiving it do not dispatch another payment
or refresh the source data.

## Read the complete application and financing

The selected package includes the manuscript author's reviewed application,
the product and financing companion, the original six-package budget and the
source index. Open them through the shared source server:

~~~sh
starforge grant-application --port 8787
~~~

Open the exact local URL printed at startup, normally
`http://127.0.0.1:8787/grant.html`. Choose `--port 0` when another service already
uses that port. If the same package's `cocart-setup` listener is already open,
read `/grant.html` at its existing origin.

The application page provides the complete original Markdown downloads,
`budget.csv`, `source-index.json`, the preserved economic briefing and the
published presentation links. The four direct local downloads are:

| Download | Local path |
| --- | --- |
| Primary application | `/grant-data/application.md` |
| Product and financing companion | `/grant-data/product-and-finance.md` |
| Six-package budget | `/grant-data/budget.csv` |
| Source and measure index | `/grant-data/source-index.json` |

The source manifest identifies the complete selected application edition.
The source index retains the underlying manuscript and financial identities;
the preceding reviewer source at `f7fe93c07355b1688a550bbcd349a5590fa1d680`
remains in the original history. Read the published film and editable
companion at the original release links. The package retains the current
application and economic-report source downloads.

Begin with **Explore the working product** to inspect the original film and
complete report, follow Applications, or prepare the same installed/source
command and complete opening guide. Its [reviewer-opening guide](../../stellar-forge/developer-site/GRANT_ENTRY.md)
travels with this selected source.

Choose **Prepare submission** to edit the nine complete answers, map the
actual issuer fields and limits, copy the selected full text, and save a
complete version. Export and reopen the working draft with every source
edition, manual answer, field mapping and review note. Receiving a later
source edition preserves manual edits against their original baselines.
The [submission operating guide](../../stellar-forge/developer-site/GRANT_SUBMISSION.md)
covers that complete original workflow.

Choose **Review prepared draft** for the original named reviewer and author
workflow. Receive the complete saved draft, record decisions and quoted change
requests, return the full review, and compare the author's next complete draft.
Carry decisions explicitly for unchanged content; changed source or answers
reopen affected review requests. The original **Submission handover** retains
that selected review with planning, prepared output and issuer observations.
The [review-round guide](../../stellar-forge/developer-site/GRANT_REVIEW_ROUNDS.md)
and [handover guide](../../stellar-forge/developer-site/GRANT_HANDOVER.md) travel
with the same installed source and draft-store workflow.

The installed `grant-compose` command receives the owner's selected manuscript
through the same maintained composer:

~~~sh
starforge grant-compose \
  --directory /absolute/current/developer-site/dist \
  --manuscript /absolute/current-scf-application.md \
  --source-pins-output /absolute/current-grant-source-pins.json
~~~

Keep the current application, complete detailed companion, source index and
page shell together in that directory. Existing product selections are
retained from the source index; the [composition guide](../../stellar-forge/developer-site/GRANT_COMPOSITION.md)
describes explicitly selecting a new economic, coastal, merchant-financial or paired Datasette source. Its [financial application guide](../../stellar-forge/developer-site/GRANT_FINANCIAL_OPERATIONS.md) covers **--finance-commit**, dated customer balances, settlement and accountant receiving within the same current application.
The four emitted reader pins go to the original `inspectGrantApplication`
callback. The selected installed renderer/projector hashes and the original
canonical-front identity remain recorded in the source index.

Ctrl+C closes this reader. Reopen the same command to read the same installed
source. For a checkout, the original entry is
`node stellar-forge/developer-site/grant.mjs --port 8787`.
The retained purchase workbench below keeps its own saved packet and lifecycle.

## Export a saved submission

The installed `grant-export` command prepares the same saved draft through the
original submission, planning and handover models:

~~~sh
starforge grant-export \
  --draft /private/scf/saved-submission.json \
  --out /private/scf/prepared-submission
~~~

Select a new private output directory. The complete result contains the native
checksummed draft for reopening, all nine canonical answers, the original form
map, prepared values and exact individual field text, an offline copy/print
page, and the final file manifest. Manual edits, source editions, planning,
review decisions and version history stay in the same native record.

Use `--select answers` or `--select fields` to select the output explicitly;
`--format plain` and `--format markdown` use the original model's prepared
values. Counts and recorded issuer limits apply to those exact values. Exit 2
retains the complete output and reports recorded limits exceeded. The
[complete export guide](../../stellar-forge/developer-site/GRANT_EXPORT.md)
also covers receiving a matching application/source-index pair with its
original URL and complete budget/companion files. Reopen `draft.json` through
**Prepare submission** to continue the same draft.

## Prepare the customer's operating procedure

The installed reviewer includes Command finder and Operating plans. A saved
submission's **Planning → Customer operating procedure** turns its selected
native SF47 packages into editable ordered work, with each original scope,
completion measure, price, hours and relative window retained.

~~~sh
starforge grant-operating-plan \
  --file /absolute/customer/submission-draft.json \
  --customer "Receiving merchant" \
  --out /absolute/customer/operating-plan.json

starforge discover serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8846
~~~

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8846/operating-plan.html` and choose **Import complete
plan**. Enter actual operating instructions, due dates and command arguments,
then save revisions as work progresses. Complete JSON transfers all saved
history; HTML and Markdown carry the readable procedure.

Use `starforge discover plan catalog --out /absolute/customer/toolkit-catalog.json`
to supply the complete actual toolkit registrations to the saved planning
review. The [customer operating procedure guide](../../stellar-forge/developer-site/GRANT_OPERATING_PLANS.md)
describes original native files, explicit package selection, catalog bindings
and receiving.

## Open the reviewer

Use the [maintained runtime installation](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/RUNTIME_INSTALL.md)
with the native Stellar packages, the `mcp` feature and operator support.
Retain its selected source archive, complete lock and READY installation.

In **Applications**, select **Grant purchase reviewer**. Choose that runtime
and a private workbench directory beneath an existing private parent. Leave
Packet and SHA-256 empty to select the bundled original purchase in the
workbench, or supply the exact receiving packet and displayed digest.

Choose **Review**, **Save**, **Connect** and **Start**, then **Open**.
The saved application binds the workbench, selected packet and runtime.
Applications opens only the current workbench instance.

The installed command opens the same product directly:

~~~sh
starforge grant-demo workbench --dir /srv/starforge/state/grant-review --port 0
~~~

For a source checkout, replace `starforge grant-demo` with
`node stellar/scf_2026/presentation/reviewer/cli.mjs`.
Keep the private parent directory under the operator's control. Structured
startup output contains the listening address and instance identity; open
through Applications or read the original local
`workbench-connection.json` for this instance's private access code.
The browser clears the entered code and URL fragment after connecting.

## Review the original source and read the complete result

1. Open **Packet intake** and choose **Review bundled purchase**, or upload the
   complete exported JSON packet. The workbench retains its exact bytes and
   checks its original documents, native result representation and SHA-256.
2. Open **Source and query**. Review the retained source, original query,
   selected terms and complete source-document downloads.
3. Choose **Receive this packet**. The original receiving engine restores the
   native quote records and full result files into this selection's private
   directory.
4. Choose **Open original Buyer**, then open **Buyer results**.
5. Select each quote and choose **Read complete saved result**. The original
   Buyer client reads every retained range and checks the complete byte count
   and digest before presenting or downloading the result.

The bundled NYC HPD purchase contains 100 building-in-project rows and
14 columns in its original 53,468-byte MCP result. Its retained truncation flag
remains true. The source vintage and exact query are shown with that result;
these are historical project events rather than a current housing listing.

The primary quote retains its confirmed seller status and matched transfer.
The earlier indeterminate quote remains separately visible with its original
failed observation and complete 4,733-byte error result. Read each original
record in its own history.

**Open original console** uses that Buyer's existing private-code form.
Retrieve and copy its current code through authenticated local access.
Keep it out of exported packets and shared project metadata.

## Export a closed Buyer and receive it elsewhere

Choose **Handover → Close Buyer and export packet**. The workbench waits for
the whole original Buyer to close, drain its work and release the writer lease.
The export then includes the complete native quote transitions and results
from that closed view.

Download the packet and retain its displayed SHA-256 with it. Give the receiving
operator the complete packet. Their new Applications review selects that
original file and digest, a new private workbench directory and their own
reviewed runtime.

The direct command uses the same receiving path:

~~~sh
starforge grant-demo workbench --dir /srv/starforge/state/received-review \
  --packet /srv/starforge/received/original-review.json \
  --sha256 ORIGINAL_EXPORTED_SHA256 --port 0
~~~

The receiving operator reviews and receives the packet, opens the native Buyer
and reads the full original results. Their private access code and workbench
are new; the original quote identities and result bytes remain the same.
**Review receiving copy** provides this same handover locally and labels that
selection as a local copy.

## Continue after closing or interruption

Use **Reopen this received packet** to start the original Buyer after a closed
export. In Applications, **Stop** drains the managed workbench and its Buyer;
the next reviewed Start reopens the same retained workspace.

Keep the workbench directory and its original action IDs. A lost response can
continue the same action with the same selected inputs. An already published
export is recovered by its original identity before current mutable Buyer
history is read. A completed Open receipt shows its historical outcome
separately from the current live Buyer.

A prepared managed start retains its original request ID before child dispatch.
Reopen the same Applications controller and recover that request. Do not
substitute a new workbench or repeat the original purchase.

The [complete reviewer operating guide](../../stellar/scf_2026/presentation/reviewer/WORKBENCH.md)
covers the original command, private access, receiving decisions and managed
continuation. Its full receiving carrier can extend the same already completed
direct journal with an actual matching READY runtime; it keeps the original
run, skips completed direct phases and preserves the earlier result.


## Operate the same review from a merchant or application client

The [merchant provider and typed client](../../stellar/scf_2026/presentation/reviewer/merchant/README.md)
connect these same workbenches to the existing merchant MCP host. Select the
full toolkit or a reviewed product selection containing both `merchant-mcp`
and the `merchant-grant-reviewer` contribution.

Save the original and receiving directories under named aliases in a private
`stellar-forge.grant-reviewer-merchant-connection.v1` JSON file. An alias with
`allowStart: false` borrows the workbench already opened by Applications;
`allowStart: true` permits an explicit start of that same original workbench.
The complete guide supplies the exact connection fields and source-file pins.

~~~sh
starforge merchant-grant-reviewer init --directory /srv/starforge/reviewer-merchant \
  --connection /srv/starforge/private/reviewer-connections.json
starforge merchant-mcp serve --config /srv/starforge/reviewer-merchant/merchant-mcp.json \
  --port 3211 --token-env MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN
~~~

The twenty `merchant_grant_reviewer_` operations provide source review and
receiving, current Buyer lifecycle, original quote/history/result reading,
complete document retrieval, closed-view export and full-file receiving.
The typed `@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/grant/reviewer-merchant` client
uses the same contracts; its CLI supports calls, local-file review, inspection,
interrupted-download continuation and local cold reopening.

Retain the request UUID with each action. After a lost reply, inspect or repeat
that original action with the same input. An exported file keeps its complete
manifest, original workbench identity, byte count and SHA-256 as the merchant
host restarts. The receiver resumes the original saved download directory and
checks every file before reopening it.

Merchant shutdown releases its readers and its own workbenches. An
Applications-owned workbench remains with that original owner. The private
Buyer code stays in its original host connection.

This standalone edition includes the complete source from
[public PR1984](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/pull/1984),
merge `ddde47d69aac27cae5021a17bc6b3d15d43fc884`. The complete
[merchant receiving continuation](../../stellar/scf_2026/presentation/reviewer/merchant/RECEIVING.mjs)
extends the same original closed reviewer operation and both saved result files.
The Console continuation follows that same operation and its existing merchant
journal through complete customer delivery and independent receiving.

## Complete customer delivery in the operator workspace

The `grant-reviewer` product selection includes both **Grant purchase reviewer**
and **Merchant operator** in Applications. Keep the original workbench open
through its owning application. Initialize its merchant connection with the
command above, then save **Merchant operator** using that
`merchant-mcp.json`, a private saved operator directory and the original token
environment name. **Review Start → Start → Open** leads to the authenticated
operator workspace on that same merchant listener.

The direct command opens the same workspace:

~~~sh
starforge merchant-mcp serve \
  --config /srv/starforge/reviewer-merchant/merchant-mcp.json \
  --operator-console-dir /srv/starforge/reviewer-merchant/operator-console \
  --port 3211 --token-env MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN
~~~

Select or create a named profile, then open **Customers → Reviewer customer
delivery**. Work through the five sections:

1. Load the configured workbench aliases and open the original source state.
2. Review the bundled purchase, a declared host file, or a complete local packet.
   Inspect the saved selection and its revision before receiving it.
3. Open the original Buyer and read its complete saved history, both quote
   outcomes, full result files and source documents.
4. Close the Buyer and export the selected packet. **Receive these original
   files** retains its complete manifest and every original file in Customers.
   Download the full receiving packet, or choose an individual retained file.
5. Prepare the complete delivery or receiving recipe. The existing Workflow
   Recipes editor reviews its actual inputs and native contracts, then installs
   a named immutable workflow edition.

The delivery recipe has fourteen native steps, with pauses at source inspection,
the complete saved result, closed export, receiving review and received history.
The six-step receiving recipe starts from an existing reviewed export. Its
destination is another configured workbench. Each original action UUID stays
with its saved request; a lost response continues that request and revision.

A completed workflow export can be reopened in Customers with its exact
workbench alias, export ID and manifest SHA-256. Receiving resumes the retained
file checkpoints after interruption. The complete packet remains
`grant-reviewer-packet.json`; its accompanying manifest and operation file are
also available individually.

**Export profile** carries the original requests, workflow installation and run,
complete customer identities and immutable host-binding history. The receiving
operator imports that history into its own retained Console, then receives the
original files from the selected export. After a host change, **Host → Review
host** compares the actual configured tools and declarations before the operator
saves the displayed binding.

The [complete Reviewer Customer Delivery guide](../../stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/console/CUSTOMER_REVIEWER.md)
includes the exact recipe inputs, response recovery, full-file controls and
original native receiving continuation. The
[Merchant operator Applications guide](../../stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/console/APPLICATIONS.md)
covers saved launch, current private Open, drained Stop and cold reopen.

## Read the scientific report-product architecture

The [development guide](../merchant-workspace/DEVELOPMENT.md#frozen-scientific-reports-as-merchant-resources)
now connects the complete Groundwater report product to the same native seller,
buyer and Operations boundaries. The upstream
[operator guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/9b6b92c2c290b73ca6e263d28603fdcad3a19bf6/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/groundwater-report/OPERATOR.md)
covers exact frozen report assets and terms, original buyer preparation,
full-package verification, an attributed file decision, optional selected-case
association and complete report-desk receiving.

Review this as a distinct delivered software capability. Its exact source,
Linux request recovery and complete control-desk restore have been verified;
its scientific report/portal operation is still being continued from the
original generated-package reference finding. A successful source check is
not a completed report sale or customer receiving decision.

The NYC HPD reviewer packet, both quote outcomes, original result bytes and
existing purchase/receiving operation above remain unchanged. Read the new
report workflow from its own actual frozen report and explicitly authorized
buyer evidence when those records are available. The
[Operations guide](../grant-operations/OPERATING.md#frozen-groundwater-report-receiving)
describes the precise case/deployment/purchase selection. Neither this
architecture addition nor opening its source creates another purchase.

### Customer commissioning calendar and complete useful jobs

The fourteen-day mainnet target needs an explicit customer calendar. On an ordinary Monday–Friday schedule without holidays, two buyers making one useful purchase each per business day produce twenty purchases in fourteen calendar days. The proposed commissioning calendar reaches thirty through fifteen independently useful jobs per buyer: ten complete source-period extracts and five separate reconciliation or reporting decisions. Both proposed merchant installations serve both buyers. The customer workorder must replace the relative dates, source periods and roles with actual customer selections before this plan can be used.

The [complete customer commissioning specification](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/33dfb64798f5316a586c165d4d7591de972ca4e2/stellar-forge/developer-site/A2A_CUSTOMER_COMMISSIONING.md) and [thirty-job register](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/33dfb64798f5316a586c165d4d7591de972ca4e2/stellar-forge/developer-site/a2a-customer-commissioning.json) name each job's purpose, period, complete output and receiving role. Buyer A's additional jobs cover new or missing observations, late corrections, asset coverage, metadata/status changes and a correction decision register. Buyer B's additional jobs deliver distinct two-period briefs, a source-quality publication, a complete first-workweek report, a selected-cohort report and a complete two-workweek publication. These are prospective customer adaptations to approved saved queries/reports; customer identities, procedure IDs, source licenses, prices, signers and receiving people remain unselected.

For each actual job, the receiving record joins the original customer approval, priced request, native settlement, A2A task, merchant request, full output byte identities and SF82 release/edition to the named receiver's decision. Useful customer jobs, priced requests, native settlements and complete received tasks are counted separately. Retries, reconnects, resumed work, several formats for one result and unnecessary repeat purchases do not create additional useful jobs. The existing development reference and team testnet baseline remain separately attributed.

The appendix preserves the existing $38,000-equivalent request, 400-hour allocation, 150-day programme and milestone definitions. Its remaining customer work fits once into the existing six funded packages, or into a separately commissioned workorder where applicable. Already completed reusable source is the selected starting component. The current manuscript and installation owners approve the actual calendar and accountabilities; this prospective plan records no executed customer outcome or payment.

# Customer commissioning for the A2A analytical product

**Status: proposed customer work specification, 12 October 2026.** This document resolves the activity cadence for the existing grant's day-150 target. It does not identify a commissioned buyer, authorize a payment, or record a completed purchase. Its machine-readable companion is [a2a-customer-commissioning.json](a2a-customer-commissioning.json). The two files describe the same thirty jobs.

The current application requests **$38,000 equivalent paid in XLM, 400 hours at a planning rate of $95/hour, over 150 days from actual award acceptance**. Its day-150 activity target is at least thirty useful purchases across two independent buyers during fourteen consecutive calendar days; both merchant installations receive independent buyer use, and both buyers return on another day. This appendix preserves those figures, the original baseline, and the other milestones. [Selected grant source index](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/6ccf9f01147418338a0fee51b38b160fdcbacc5f/stellar-forge/developer-site/dist/grant-data/source-index.json).

## An achievable calendar requires additional useful work

With an ordinary Monday–Friday calendar and no holidays, fourteen calendar days contain ten business days. One purchase from each of two buyers on each business day produces twenty purchases. Reaching thirty under that assumption requires ten additional useful purchases.

This proposed schedule gives each buyer **ten distinct source-period extracts plus five separate reconciliation or reporting jobs**. There are three planned purchases on each of ten business days, fifteen per buyer. Source-query merchant M1 serves both buyers for twenty extracts. Comparison/report merchant M2 serves both buyers for ten additional jobs. The distribution is 20/10 across merchants; the grant does not require equal purchase totals at each installation.

Every extra job must have its own customer decision, selected inputs, complete output and accountable receiving person. Repeating an already received query, splitting its CSV/JSONL/SQLite formats into separate purchases, or buying an unnecessary report does not establish a new useful job. If a proposed task is unnecessary, the customer and current application owner must choose an actually useful schedule or acknowledge that this illustration does not satisfy the target. The [original commissioning and economics brief](https://tokenjunkielabs.slack.com/docs/T0BRETUB5TK/F0C8G8A9B7V) gives the same cadence issue and calls for an actual two-week operating calendar.

Before the window begins, replace the relative days below with the customers' actual UTC dates, holidays, source periods and receiving availability. A Monday start is an illustration, not a condition imposed on customers. The first seven-day testnet milestone needs its own approved ten-purchase calendar and separate native settlement records; these planned mainnet jobs do not count retrospectively toward it.

## Customer and merchant responsibilities

| Plan label | Prospective role | Selection needed before commissioning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Buyer A | An operational monitoring customer that needs complete period extracts and actionable source-change reviews | Independent organization; actual buyer and receiving people; approved asset population; source licenses; workorder; price and payment authority |
| Buyer B | An independent analytical customer that needs complete portfolio data and scheduled publications | Separate organization; actual buyer and receiving people; approved portfolio and cohorts; client decision periods; source licenses; workorder; price and payment authority |
| Merchant M1 | A source-query merchant exposing reviewed analytical procedures | Actual independent operator and installation; approved saved queries/views; source custody; service URL; asset, signer and settlement recipient |
| Merchant M2 | A comparison/report merchant exposing reviewed reconciliation queries and publications | Actual independent operator and installation; permitted source transfer; saved comparison queries and reports; source/input editions; service URL; payment configuration |

These roles are prospective. Two actor accounts created by the development team do not establish two independent customer buyers, and two local copies of a development service do not establish the two independent merchant installations. The customer workorder records those facts and the actual operating people. Authority remains with the existing buyer approval and merchant payment paths described in the [merchant operator guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/a2a/OPERATOR.md).

## Complete job register

P01–P10 mean ten distinct customer-selected source periods. P00 is an already available, licensed baseline needed for the first comparison. Before approving any job, record each period's exact UTC boundaries and immutable source edition/hash. The two buyers select their own populations; using the same period label does not imply the same customer dataset.

For every primary A-Q job, Buyer A receives all observations for its approved asset population in the selected period, including original identifiers, nulls and source-native status. Its operational data owner accepts the result for updating the operating record. For every primary B-Q job, Buyer B receives all observations for its separately approved portfolio in that period. Its analytical data owner accepts the result for the scheduled customer analysis.

The machine-readable register contains the complete purpose, selection, source periods, output contract and receiving role for every job. ### The ten additional decision tasks

| Job | Decision supported | Required receiving input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A-C01 | Which monitored assets need a source follow-up after the first period? | Every added/missing observation key between P00 and P01, both original editions, and the approved asset population |
| A-C03 | Does the operational record need correction for late or changed observations? | All late arrivals and changed values for P02/P03, with original and current values |
| A-C05 | Which assets have newly lost or gained source coverage? | Complete asset-level coverage changes for P04/P05 and the exact population |
| A-C07 | Do metadata, unit or source quality-status changes affect combining periods? | Every changed approved metadata/status field and affected observation key for P06/P07 |
| A-C09 | Which changed records need an accept, retain or follow-up decision? | Complete correction-decision input for P08/P09; the customer retains its own decisions |
| B-R02 | What does the first two-period client brief need to say? | The complete approved report and all supporting tables for P01/P02 |
| B-R04 | Is the next two-period source sufficiently understood for the customer's analysis? | Full coverage/missing-value publication for P03/P04, with original limitations and tables |
| B-R06 | What is the completed first-workweek position? | The complete five-period publication, supporting tables and exact source inventory |
| B-R08 | How do the two customer-approved site cohorts compare? | The complete selected-cohort publication for P06–P08 and exact cohort membership |
| B-R10 | What is the position for the scheduled two-workweek customer decision? | The complete ten-period publication, all tables, original report definition and source editions |

These are requirements for customer adaptation. The released native service runs reviewed saved queries and reports selected from the original AnalysisWorkspace. It does not infer the customer's comparison rules or execute arbitrary SQL supplied by an external agent. The existing demonstration's parameter-boundary query is a receiving exercise, not an additional useful customer purchase. The retained 28-response/660-row Hamburg population is a reference input and must not be relabeled as thirty new customer tasks. The JSON companion supplies the complete record template.

Unknown payment outcomes follow the original reconciliation path and keep the same request; they do not authorize a second purchase. The application owner evaluates the actual milestone record against the grant's requirements.

# AgentSmith buyer receiving page

The public [AgentSmith receiving page](https://agentsmith-receiving.tokenjunkielabs.chatgpt.site) turns the retained AgentSmith HTTP source into a complete portable preparation and runs the maintained buyer and Freighter wallet from that preparation.

## Product flow

Open the page, review the original unpaid POST and advertised payment choices, and choose a new absolute private directory on the receiving Linux host. Keep one stable operation ID. The actual Freighter public payer can be selected now or supplied when the original operator is initialized.

**Save editable draft** writes setup-input.json, including the exact source text. **Open saved draft** restores that preparation. **Download receiving packet** writes a nine-file ZIP using the existing onboarding.mjs ZIP implementation.

| Packet file | Role |
| --- | --- |
| source-http.json | Complete original request and both HTTP response captures |
| request.json | Exact UTF-8 request bytes |
| capture.py | Maintained original capture and native preparation program |
| buyer.mjs | Receiving runner that calls the original buyer and wallet commands |
| packet.json | Operation settings and source/program digests |
| setup-input.json | Complete editable receiving draft |
| INSTALL.json | Native command arrays and their shell rendering |
| README.md | Runtime, preparation, execution and reopen guide |
| LICENSE | Original MIT license and attribution |

The original offer decoder remains offer.mjs. The native capture program is retained from **stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/partners/agentsmith/capture.py** at source **aea13f36c6bddf09fcc16cc3825094d1d30cfbb9**, SHA-256 **93214bc738c9ad92c70aadddb07655d86ea7e304ea7ed1afda0e5c6b4a940098**.

## Receiving runtime

Use Linux, Node.js **22.16 or later**, Python **3.11 or later**, and the complete existing toolkit checkout or installed source package. The runner accepts a checkout root, an installed package root containing source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009, or that component directory in its original layout.

Include the **native** and **freighter-wallet** runtime features. The native engine uses the maintained x402 2.28.0 source, Stellar SDK satisfying ^16.3.0, and the official **@stellar/freighter-api 6.0.1** in the same dependency tree. The operator browser needs the Freighter extension.

For an existing application that manages its own toolkit dependencies:

~~~sh
npm install --save-exact @stellar/freighter-api@6.0.1
starforge doctor --native --feature freighter-wallet
~~~

The wallet source contract is sf103-native-buyer-signer/browser-wallet/README.md and cli.mjs at merged source **c3f1f9a930e1a4b08a6d60f5643b98ba2f4a0e1d**. Its installed alias is **starforge browser-wallet**.

## Original commands behind the packet

The packet runner retains receiving.json in the chosen operation directory and verifies its original packet identity. The following are the underlying source commands, with explicit absolute paths substituted for the receiver.

~~~sh
python3 capture.py restore \
  --source /private/packet/source-http.json \
  --directory /private/operation/source

python3 capture.py prepare \
  --capture /private/operation/source \
  --checkout /absolute/original/checkout \
  --directory /private/operation/request \
  --intent-id ORIGINAL_STABLE_OPERATION_ID \
  --node /absolute/path/to/node

node /absolute/original/checkout/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf88-operator-buyer-cli/cli.mjs \
  --review --config /private/operation/request/review.json

node /absolute/original/checkout/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf88-operator-buyer-cli/cli.mjs \
  --init-workspace --config /private/operation/request/review.json \
  --dir /private/operation/operator \
  --actor ORIGINAL_OPERATOR_ID --service agentsmith-metar \
  --payer ACTUAL_FREIGHTER_PUBLIC_ACCOUNT \
  --python /absolute/path/to/python3

node /absolute/original/checkout/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf103-native-buyer-signer/browser-wallet/cli.mjs prepare \
  --buyer-config /private/operation/operator/operator.json \
  --out /private/operation/wallet

node /absolute/original/checkout/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf103-native-buyer-signer/browser-wallet/cli.mjs serve \
  --workspace /private/operation/wallet
~~~

Open the original wallet service's printed loopback URL in the intended browser and connect Freighter. In a second terminal:

~~~sh
node /absolute/original/checkout/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf103-native-buyer-signer/browser-wallet/cli.mjs execute \
  --workspace /private/operation/wallet \
  --operator-workspace /private/operation/operator
~~~

The original terminal approval and native authorization entry belong to this operation. Its useful merchant response remains at **/private/operation/request/metar-result.json**. Inspect the retained wallet using the original command:

~~~sh
node /absolute/original/checkout/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf103-native-buyer-signer/browser-wallet/cli.mjs inspect \
  --workspace /private/operation/wallet
~~~

The packet's **inspect** also reopens the retained capture and reviewed request, reviews the original operator if present, and reports the saved response path and size. Repeating **prepare** completes an interrupted source restoration or native preparation in the same directory. Complete private files are published atomically and reused only when their original bytes match. The original SF88 preparer derives the expected configuration before reopening a retained draft, preserving the request, stable intent and response destination. A private operation lock prevents concurrent writers.

Repeating **operator-init** invokes the maintained initializer's resume operation when its original initialization is incomplete, then checks the complete source configuration, actor, service, payer and exact request bytes. Wallet actions make those same checks before entering the original provider. The receiving manifest is created atomically, and an empty original receiving directory can finish its first creation.

The runner forwards SIGINT and SIGTERM until the native child closes and returns the child's exit status. Repeating **wallet-prepare** inspects the existing wallet. Interrupted execution continues through the original buyer and wallet recovery commands with its retained ledger and keys.

## Site integration

The additive receiving assets live in the existing **dist/** tree:

- agentsmith.html, agentsmith.css and agentsmith-setup.mjs.
- agentsmith-onboarding.mjs and agentsmith-runner.mjs.
- agentsmith-capture.py, agentsmith-source-http.json and agentsmith-LICENSE.txt.

The page imports the existing offer.mjs and onboarding.mjs. Shared styles come from style.css. The home navigation adds the same-origin AgentSmith buyer route. The page uses the existing grayscale industrial layout, explicit form labels, responsive panels, text-only source display, and local draft/ZIP downloads.

The standalone customer receiving page is published at **https://agentsmith-receiving.tokenjunkielabs.chatgpt.site** under the Bryce / TokenJunkieLabs Sites account, public project **appgprj_6acc430d195c8191a124909673496433**. Its first deployed source is **6f4ec6a14ff9f62464d2e356c5d5751289c9ab8c**, version **appgver_b6c72a5528308191a33f0bc44c2b89c6**. Future AgentSmith customer page updates use the dedicated receiving project's original source and hosting binding. Send customers the branded receiving URL.

# CoCart customer setup in the existing Starforge Site

The CoCart page turns a merchant’s saved product profile or a complete existing
customer receiving export into a portable setup package for the original
CoCart managed application. It joins the same Starforge Site, the existing
WooCommerce setup and the maintained merchant runtime.

Customer entry: **/cocart.html**. The original Site project remains
**appgprj_6acba66ca7a08191897b5a8c22611397**. Its publisher must preserve the
current audience and continue the same project and source repository.

## Customer workflow

1. Import **Download saved headless profile** from the original mapped Woo
   product, or import the complete CoCart receiving JSON from the preceding
   operator. The receiving input includes its original workspace and all
   referenced objects.
2. Optionally declare existing Woo handoffs and additional receiving files
   under distinct merchant aliases. For initial profile creation, a separate
   transport JSON can select the actual loopback receiving store and checkout.
3. Choose the real private customer directory, optional SDK entry, merchant
   connection and merchant agent directory.
4. Review the saved product, currency, exact decimal/atomic amounts, route,
   original source bytes and receiving history.
5. Download the complete ZIP. It contains original input bytes, setup.json,
   the source-native runner and a complete installation/operation handover.
6. Run Inspect and Prepare against the selected maintained toolkit. Open the
   original application, or select the same directory in managed Applications.
7. Operate the actual cart and Woo checkout, attach the original handoff,
   export the complete customer workspace, Stop and reopen the same work.

The source-native profile selects CoCart Community 4.9.7, its original v2 API,
and @cocartheadless/sdk 1.2.1. The original CoCart application requires Node 22
or later. The current profile’s checkout comparison selects one mapped simple
virtual product at quantity one with its exact saved total and Stellar terms.
The existing Woo setup also supports its separately maintained basket,
refund and merchant workflows; this page retains the CoCart source’s own
selected contract.

## Complete page and portable package

| Source | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| dist/cocart.html | Accessible original-file, host, review and operating steps. |
| dist/cocart.css | Existing industrial typography and neutral palette, including narrow screens. |
| dist/cocart-setup.mjs | File intake, saved draft lifecycle, local review, downloads and command presentation. |
| dist/cocart-onboarding.mjs | Byte-preserving source selection, packet manifest, exact local hashes and complete generated installation guide. |
| dist/cocart-runner.mjs | Portable forwarding to the original managed/native validators, setup, console, receiving export and profile companion. |
| dist/onboarding.mjs | Existing deterministic ZIP writer; imported files remain byte arrays. |
| dist/drafts.mjs | Existing IndexedDB transactions and expected-revision saves. |

The page recognizes native file formats and verifies their original lengths
and SHA-256 hashes. Full semantic validation stays with the original installed
workspace, receiving and buyer modules. The runner imports those modules from
the selected complete checkout or installed source package. It does not
implement a second cart, payment, session, native receiving or Applications
engine.

Saved browser drafts use **stellar-forge.frontdoor-cocart.v1**. The original
merchant draft store keeps CoCart rows under their own ID prefix. Saving an
existing draft supplies its expected revision to the same transactional writer.
An original newer tab edition is preserved; Save as new retains an intentional
separate draft. JSON download/open carries all original file bytes independently
of browser storage.

## Exact packet contract

The generated **stellar-forge.frontdoor-cocart-packet.v1** manifest contains:

- Operator-selected label, customer directory, optional SDK entry, private
  connection, workspace alias and optional merchant agent directory.
- Every original input’s role, native kind, optional merchant alias, canonical
  packet path, original display name, byte count and SHA-256.
- The selected native source path and plugin/SDK contract.
- A display projection of the imported profile or receiving workspace.

The ZIP includes each input as its original bytes, not reserialized JSON.
No payment key, signer selection or credential value is requested by the page.
Native profiles can contain public merchant payment terms, while customer
receiving files can contain private guest cart and order data. Browser processing
and chosen local saves stay in the operator’s browser. Deployment packages
contain only these source files.

The input capacity is the native 64 MiB per regular file, with the existing
Woo buyer handoff limited to 64 KiB. A page setup accepts at most 96 MiB across
its selected files, sixteen named Woo handoffs and sixteen named receiving
inputs. A primary receiving export retains the original alias reserved by
native managed setup.

Profile byte-order marks are rejected consistently with the original
workspace’s exact JSON source comparison. Valid UTF-8, CRLF, non-ASCII text
and original numeric lexemes remain unchanged in the copied files. Amounts
in the review are source strings; the page performs no floating-point price
conversion.

## Native runner

Run from the extracted setup folder:

~~~sh
TOOLKIT=/absolute/path/to/checkout-or-installed-package

node cocart.mjs inspect --toolkit "$TOOLKIT"
node cocart.mjs prepare --toolkit "$TOOLKIT"
node cocart.mjs status --toolkit "$TOOLKIT"

node cocart.mjs open --toolkit "$TOOLKIT"
# Use the original private URL printed by the listener.
# Ctrl+C stops this direct listener.

node cocart.mjs export --toolkit "$TOOLKIT" \
  --out /absolute/private/CoCart_Receiving_Workspace.json
~~~

**Inspect** reads the original manifest and every regular input with
no-follow file opens, checks stable file identity and exact saved hashes,
then invokes validateProfile, inspectReceiving and validateHandoff in the
original selected source. It resolves and checks the real SDK before native
setup writes. The result includes actual source, SDK, input and original
receiving identities.

**Prepare** calls setupCocartWorkspace. A native profile creates or reopens its
original workspace; a receiving export preserves the original complete
workspace and source objects. Optional named files enter the native merchant
connection. An optional merchant agent directory is initialized by the existing
shared merchant provider. After native setup, the runner checks the same input
identities and selected profile bytes again. The original receiving marker validates
the first imported revision; repeating Prepare retains later native customer changes
and reports both the input export's version and the current workspace version.

A profile packet may retain its original creation transport on repeated Prepare.
The native setup checks that declaration against its original recorded creation
selection, keeps the same connection metadata and leaves later transport rebinds,
cart revisions and history intact. Changing the current transport remains the
original explicit transport.rebind action.

The real parent of the customer workspace must exist. A missing selected
connection parent can be created as mode 0700 only under a real existing
parent. Existing directory and connection permissions are inspected and
retained. Native setup preserves a differing original connection or receiving
destination and reports the actual conflict.

**Open** forwards to the original managed console entry with the same selected
directory, SDK, connection and alias. The original entry owns its listener and
signal shutdown. Native cart requests and checkout are explicit customer
application actions.

**Status** rereads the native workspace without selecting a different cart or
order. **Export** uses CartWorkspace.receivingBundle and validates the complete
original receiving envelope before writing an exclusive private output.
Existing differing output bytes are preserved; choose a new filename for
a subsequent export. The actual returned revision, workspace version,
receiving digest, cart count and object count identify the result.

## First Woo installation

The existing **/woo.html** page remains the complete SF104 plugin,
merchant connection, seller, continuous SF98 delivery and buyer handover.
This page adds the original CoCart profile-export companion:

~~~sh
node cocart.mjs plugin --toolkit "$TOOLKIT" \
  --out /absolute/private/new-profile-plugin
~~~

The plugin preparation can run without setup.json. It copies the exact
original **profile-export.php** as **starforge-cocart-profile.php**, plus
the original CoCart, managed and gateway guides. Each copied file is hashed
and read back. The selected directory and existing differing files are
preserved.

Install and activate that companion in the existing Woo shop alongside its
selected CoCart, WooCommerce and SF104 plugins. Save the actual merchant
mapping, then download the product’s saved headless profile. The companion
uses the native Woo nonce and product-edit permissions.

## Original managed Applications and merchant agent

The generated handover names the actual existing Applications fields:

| Applications field | Setup source |
| --- | --- |
| workspaceDirectory | The original customer directory. |
| sdkModule | Optional explicit original SDK entry. |
| connectionFile | Optional same-workspace native merchant connection. |
| workspaceAlias | Its original selected alias. |
| Local port | The existing common setting; zero selects an available loopback port. |

Review, Save, Review start, Start and Open use the existing application
manager. The original CoCart preparer pins selected source, SDK and workspace
identity. Its serialized observer checks the actual token-bound listener
before retaining Open. Stop and reopen stay in that same original manager.

The optional native merchant configuration uses the existing
cocartWorkspaceConnection field. The provider and browser select the same
CartWorkspace; named inputs remain original host files. Setup declares
handoffs for subsequent explicit actions and does not attach a handoff to a
made-up checkout preview.

## Customer acceptance and support

The complete generated INSTALL.md connects the installer’s setup to the
customer’s operating handover:

- Selected shop, source, SDK, product and merchant mapping.
- Actual catalog, cart mutation and checkout behavior.
- Original order, attempt generation and buyer handoff.
- Existing seller and delivery operator.
- Complete receiving export, original revision and source objects.
- Managed Stop, reopen and continued access to the same customer history.
- Named operating owner, backup destination and support contact.

The same exported case supplies the support context for a returned cart,
checkout or handoff issue. A source update, local port change or new merchant
mapping is handled through the original selected product operation and
its recorded reason/version.

            stream.write(data)
            stream.flush()
            os.fsync(stream.fileno())
        os.link(temporary, path, follow_symlinks=False)
        directory_fd = os.open(path.parent, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY)
        try:
            os.fsync(directory_fd)
        finally:
            os.close(directory_fd)
    finally:
        if owned:
            temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)


def retain_exact(path, data):
    """Reuse completed bytes directly, including on a nearly full filesystem."""
    try:
        fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        try:
            write_new(path, data)
            return
        except FileExistsError:
            fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
    with os.fdopen(fd, "rb") as stream:
        info = os.fstat(stream.fileno())
        need(stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) and not info.st_mode & 0o077
             and info.st_size == len(data), "Retained file differs: " + path.name)
        need(stream.read(len(data) + 1) == data, "Retained bytes differ: " + path.name)


@contextmanager
def output_operation(directory):
    directory.mkdir(mode=0o700, exist_ok=True)
    info = directory.lstat()
    need(stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode) and not info.st_mode & 0o077
         and info.st_uid == os.getuid(), "Use the original private output directory")
    fd = os.open(directory / ".receiving.lock",
                 os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600)
    try:
        lock_info = os.fstat(fd)
        need(stat.S_ISREG(lock_info.st_mode) and not lock_info.st_mode & 0o077,
             "Original receiving lock must be private")
        try:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        except BlockingIOError:
            raise ValueError("The original receiving operation is already running")
        yield
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


class NoRedirect(HTTPRedirectHandler):
    def redirect_request(self, req, fp, code, msg, headers, newurl):
        return None


def read_http(url, method, body=None):
    req = Request(https(url), data=body, method=method,
                  headers={"Accept": "application/json",
                           "Content-Type": "application/json",
                           "User-Agent": "TokenJunkieLabs-AgentSmith-Integration/1.0"})
    try:
        response = build_opener(NoRedirect()).open(req, timeout=25)
    except HTTPError as error:
        response = error
    with response:
        data = response.read(MAX_CAPTURE + 1)
        need(len(data) <= MAX_CAPTURE, "Response exceeds capture limit")
        return {"url": url, "method": method,
                "retrievedAt": dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).isoformat(),
                "status": response.status,
                "headers": dict((k.lower(), v) for k, v in response.headers.items()),
                "bodyUtf8": data.decode("utf-8"), "bodySha256": sha(data)}


def select_offer(challenge, url):
    need(challenge.get("x402Version") == 2, "x402 version 2 required")
    need(challenge.get("resource", {}).get("url") == url,
         "Original challenge resource must match the requested URL exactly")
    offers = challenge.get("accepts")
    need(isinstance(offers, list) and 0 < len(offers) <= 32, "Original offers required")
    selected = []
    for index, offer in enumerate(offers):
        if (offer.get("scheme") == "exact" and offer.get("network") == NETWORK
                and offer.get("asset") == ASSET
                and offer.get("extra", {}).get("areFeesSponsored") is True):
            need(re.fullmatch(r"[1-9][0-9]*", str(offer.get("amount", ""))),
                 "Positive atomic amount required")
            need(re.fullmatch(r"[GC][A-Z2-7]{55}", str(offer.get("payTo", ""))),
                 "Stellar recipient required")
            need(type(offer.get("maxTimeoutSeconds")) is int
                 and 1 <= offer["maxTimeoutSeconds"] <= 86400,
                 "Native authorization lifetime required")
            need(offer.get("extra", {}).get("paymentFlow", "authorization") == "authorization",
                 "This receiving recipe selects authorization payment flow")
            selected.append(index)
    need(len(selected) == 1, "Exactly one sponsored exact testnet USDC offer required")
    return selected[0]


def capture(args):
    directory = Path(args.directory).resolve()
    directory.mkdir(mode=0o700)
    body = Path(args.body_file).read_bytes() if args.body_file else encoded({"icao": args.icao})
    need(0 < len(body) <= 16777216, "Native request must contain 1 byte to 16 MiB")
    request_json = json.loads(body)
    need(isinstance(request_json, dict), "The selected JSON request must be an object")
    write_new(directory / "request.json", body)
    supported = read_http(args.facilitator.rstrip("/") + "/supported", "GET")
    write_new(directory / "supported.http.json", encoded(supported))
    response = read_http(args.url, "POST", body)
    response["requestBodySha256"] = sha(body)
    response["requestBodyBytes"] = len(body)
    write_new(directory / "challenge.http.json", encoded(response))
    return complete_capture(directory, body, supported, response, args.url, args.facilitator)


def complete_capture(directory, body, supported, response, url, facilitator, *, resume=False):
    retain = retain_exact if resume else write_new
    need(supported["status"] == 200, "Facilitator supported response must be HTTP 200")
    kinds = json.loads(supported["bodyUtf8"]).get("kinds", [])
    need(any(k.get("x402Version") == 2 and k.get("scheme") == "exact"
             and k.get("network") == NETWORK
             and k.get("extra", {}).get("areFeesSponsored") is True for k in kinds),
         "Facilitator must advertise sponsored exact Stellar testnet")
    need(response["status"] == 402, "Seller must return the actual unpaid HTTP 402")
    header = response["headers"].get("payment-required", "")
    need(0 < len(header) <= 262144, "Original PAYMENT-REQUIRED header required")
    challenge_bytes = base64.b64decode(header, validate=True)
    challenge = json.loads(challenge_bytes)
    index = select_offer(challenge, url)
    retain(directory / "payment-required.json", challenge_bytes)
    # Only the envelope changes. Preserve the entire original challenge as its row.
    retain(directory / "offers.json", encoded({"resources": [challenge]}))
    names = ["request.json", "supported.http.json", "challenge.http.json",
             "payment-required.json", "offers.json"]
    manifest = {"schema": SCHEMA, "seller": url, "method": "POST",
                "facilitator": facilitator, "network": NETWORK,
                "capturedAt": response["retrievedAt"], "rowIndex": 0,
                "acceptIndex": index, "selectedOffer": challenge["accepts"][index],
                "files": {name: {"sha256": sha((directory / name).read_bytes()),
                                 "bytes": (directory / name).stat().st_size} for name in names}}
    retain(directory / "capture.json", encoded(manifest))
    return {"status": "ORIGINAL_HTTP_SOURCE_CAPTURED", "directory": str(directory),
            "manifestSha256": sha((directory / "capture.json").read_bytes()),
            "selectedOffer": manifest["selectedOffer"]}


def restore(args):
    bundle = json.loads(Path(args.source).read_bytes())
    need(bundle.get("schema") == "commons.agentsmith.http-bundle.v1",
         "Original AgentSmith HTTP bundle required")
    supported, response = bundle["supported"], bundle["challenge"]
    body = bundle["requestUtf8"].encode("utf-8")
    need(response["requestBodySha256"] == sha(body)
         and response["requestBodyBytes"] == len(body), "Original request bytes changed")
    need(supported["bodySha256"] == sha(supported["bodyUtf8"].encode("utf-8"))
         and response["bodySha256"] == sha(response["bodyUtf8"].encode("utf-8")),
         "Original HTTP response bytes changed")
    url, facilitator = https(bundle["seller"]), https(bundle["facilitator"])
    need(response["url"] == url and response["method"] == "POST"
         and supported["url"] == facilitator.rstrip("/") + "/supported"
         and supported["method"] == "GET", "Original HTTP sources changed")
    directory = Path(args.directory).absolute()
    need(directory.resolve() == directory, "Use the original unaliased capture path")
    with output_operation(directory):
        retain_exact(directory / "request.json", body)
        retain_exact(directory / "supported.http.json", encoded(supported))
        retain_exact(directory / "challenge.http.json", encoded(response))
        return complete_capture(directory, body, supported, response, url, facilitator, resume=True)


def read_capture(directory):
    root = Path(directory).resolve()
    manifest = json.loads((root / "capture.json").read_bytes())
    need(manifest.get("schema") == SCHEMA, "Original capture schema required")
    for name, expected in manifest["files"].items():
        need(Path(name).name == name, "Capture file must remain inside its directory")
        data = (root / name).read_bytes()
        need(len(data) == expected["bytes"] and sha(data) == expected["sha256"],
             "Retained source bytes changed: " + name)
    response = json.loads((root / "challenge.http.json").read_bytes())
    body = (root / "request.json").read_bytes()
    need(response["status"] == 402 and response["requestBodySha256"] == sha(body)
         and response["requestBodyBytes"] == len(body), "Original HTTP request binding changed")
    challenge = json.loads((root / "payment-required.json").read_bytes())
    need(base64.b64decode(response["headers"]["payment-required"], validate=True)
         == (root / "payment-required.json").read_bytes(), "Original header bytes changed")
    need(json.loads((root / "offers.json").read_bytes()) == {"resources": [challenge]},
         "Native saved offer must carry the complete original challenge")
    index = select_offer(challenge, manifest["seller"])
    need(index == manifest["acceptIndex"]
         and challenge["accepts"][index] == manifest["selectedOffer"],
         "Selected source terms changed")
    return root, manifest


PREPARE_REVIEW_JS = """
import {readFile} from 'node:fs/promises';
import {pathToFileURL} from 'node:url';
const {prepareReview} = await import(pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href);
const result = prepareReview(await readFile(process.argv[2]), JSON.parse(process.argv[3]));
process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({configSha256:result.configSha256,
    dataBase64:result.data.toString('base64')}));
"""


def prepare(args):
    root, manifest = read_capture(args.capture)
    checkout = Path(args.checkout).resolve()
    cli = checkout / NATIVE
    need(cli.is_file(), "Complete Commons checkout and original SF88 CLI required")
    need(re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}", args.intent_id), "Stable intent ID required")
    output = Path(args.directory).absolute()
    need(output.resolve() == output, "Use the original unaliased request path")
    body = (root / "request.json").read_bytes()
    review_path = output / "review.json"
    record_path = output / "preparation.json"
    with output_operation(output):
        retain_exact(output / "request.json", body)
        # The original pure preparer binds a pre-existing draft before resuming
        # around the original create-only CLI. Request/output paths stay fixed.
        selection = {"rowIndex": manifest["rowIndex"], "acceptIndex": manifest["acceptIndex"],
                     "intentId": args.intent_id, "url": manifest["seller"], "method": "POST",
                     "bodyFile": str(output / "request.json"), "bodyBytes": len(body),
                     "bodySha256": sha(body), "headers": {"Content-Type": "application/json"},
                     "responseOut": str(output / "metar-result.json")}
        derived = subprocess.run(
            [args.node, "--input-type=module", "-e", PREPARE_REVIEW_JS,
             str(cli.parent / "prepare.mjs"), str(root / "offers.json"),
             json.dumps(selection)], cwd=checkout, check=True, text=True, capture_output=True)
        expected = json.loads(derived.stdout)
        config_bytes = base64.b64decode(expected["dataBase64"], validate=True)
        need(sha(config_bytes) == expected["configSha256"], "Original preparer result changed")
        prior_record = json.loads(record_path.read_bytes()) if record_path.exists() else None
        if prior_record is not None:
            need(prior_record.get("schema") == "commons.agentsmith.native-preparation.v1"
                 and prior_record.get("intentId") == args.intent_id
                 and prior_record.get("sourceDirectory") == str(root)
                 and prior_record.get("captureManifestSha256") == sha((root / "capture.json").read_bytes())
                 and prior_record.get("reviewConfigSha256") == sha(config_bytes),
                 "Reopen the original preparation and its stable intent")
        native_path = output / "native-prepare.json"
        if review_path.exists():
            retain_exact(review_path, config_bytes)
            if native_path.exists():
                native_result = json.loads(native_path.read_bytes())
                need(native_result.get("configPath") == str(review_path)
                     and native_result.get("configSha256") == sha(config_bytes),
                     "Original preparation result differs")
            else:
                # This is the actual original prepareReview result after a
                # completed draft survived interruption before its stdout saved.
                native_result = {"mode": "OFFLINE_CONFIG_REOPENED",
                                 "configPath": str(review_path),
                                 "configSha256": expected["configSha256"],
                                 "intentId": args.intent_id,
                                 "sourceFileSha256": sha((root / "offers.json").read_bytes())}
                retain_exact(native_path, encoded(native_result))
        else:
            need(prior_record is None and not native_path.exists(),
                 "Restore the original reviewed configuration before continuing")
            argv = [args.node, str(cli), "--prepare", "--discovery", str(root / "offers.json"),
                    "--row", str(manifest["rowIndex"]), "--accept", str(manifest["acceptIndex"]),
                    "--intent-id", args.intent_id, "--url", manifest["seller"], "--method", "POST",
                    "--body-file", str(output / "request.json"), "--content-type", "application/json",
                    "--response-out", str(output / "metar-result.json"), "--out", str(review_path)]
            result = subprocess.run(argv, cwd=checkout, check=True, text=True, capture_output=True)
            native_result = json.loads(result.stdout)
            retain_exact(review_path, config_bytes)
            retain_exact(native_path, encoded(native_result))
        reviewed = subprocess.run(
            [args.node, str(cli), "--review", "--config", str(review_path)],
            cwd=checkout, check=True, text=True, capture_output=True)
        review = json.loads(reviewed.stdout)
        review_result = output / "native-review.json"
        if not review_result.exists():
            retain_exact(review_result, encoded(review))
        record = {"schema": "commons.agentsmith.native-preparation.v1",
                  "captureManifestSha256": sha((root / "capture.json").read_bytes()),
                  "checkout": str(checkout), "nativeCliSha256": sha(cli.read_bytes()),
                  "intentId": args.intent_id, "sourceDirectory": str(root),
                  "reviewConfig": str(review_path), "nativeResult": native_result,
                  "reviewConfigSha256": sha(config_bytes)}
        if prior_record is None:
            retain_exact(record_path, encoded(record))
        return {"status": "NATIVE_BUYER_REVIEW_REOPENED" if prior_record else "NATIVE_BUYER_REVIEW_PREPARED",
                "directory": str(output), "config": str(review_path),
                "intentId": args.intent_id, "nativeReview": review}


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    capt = sub.add_parser("capture", help="Retain the actual facilitator and unpaid seller response")
    capt.add_argument("--directory", required=True)
    capt.add_argument("--url", type=https, default=SELLER)
    capt.add_argument("--facilitator", type=https, default=FACILITATOR)
    request = capt.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    request.add_argument("--body-file")
    request.add_argument("--icao", default="KJFK")
    prep = sub.add_parser("prepare", help="Call the original SF88 prepare and review commands")
    prep.add_argument("--capture", required=True)
    prep.add_argument("--checkout", required=True)
    prep.add_argument("--directory", required=True)
    prep.add_argument("--intent-id", required=True)
    prep.add_argument("--node", default="node")
    rest = sub.add_parser("restore", help="Receive a retained original HTTP bundle offline")
    rest.add_argument("--source", required=True)
    rest.add_argument("--directory", required=True)
    ins = sub.add_parser("inspect", help="Reopen and inspect the same retained source")
    ins.add_argument("--capture", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.command == "capture":
        result = capture(args)
    elif args.command == "prepare":
        result = prepare(args)
    elif args.command == "restore":
        result = restore(args)
    else:
        root, manifest = read_capture(args.capture)
        result = {"directory": str(root), **manifest}
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        main()
    except (OSError, ValueError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as error:
        if isinstance(error, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
            print(error.stderr.strip(), file=sys.stderr)
        print(json.dumps({"error": type(error).__name__, "message": str(error),
                          "recovery": "Continue from the same retained capture and original intent."}),
              file=sys.stderr)
        raise SystemExit(1)

# Open the U.S. economic briefing

Open [the complete economic report](stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/fred/examples/briefing-20261012/briefing.html) in your browser. It works offline and carries its original observations, comparisons and source notes. No account, API key or merchant connection is required to read this saved edition.

## Read and reuse the report

The **Summary** tab shows the latest available observation in each selected series. **Measures** contains all 150 comparisons; select a series or calculation state to inspect its original current value, baseline, dates and units. **Sources & method** carries publisher metadata and the actual public-table retrieval dates. The report's **Download all measures** and **Download report data** buttons save the complete CSV and JSON locally.

The reporting window is January 2024 through September 2026. The full source has 2,219 observations; this report selects 75 and retains all 103 current/baseline observations needed for its comparisons. Of the 150 comparisons, 144 have both values, four retain a missing current value and two retain a missing baseline. Original missing values remain visible.

This is a retained October 2026 source edition. Its public-table retrieval basis is preserved; it is not an ALFRED historical-vintage selection or a live economic feed. Read each series' own source update and retrieval time before reusing its values.

| Series | How to read its changes |
| --- | --- |
| UNRATE | Original unemployment rate in percent. Absolute differences are **percentage points**. Relative percent change was not selected. |
| CPIAUCSL | Original monthly seasonally adjusted price index. Absolute differences keep the index units; relative changes use the selected exact period ratio. |
| GDP | Original nominal quarterly GDP in billions of dollars at a seasonally adjusted annual rate. The relative comparison is the direct ratio of the two published levels; it is not an annualized growth rate or real GDP growth. |

Absolute changes use exact decimal subtraction. Relative changes use the separately selected ratio and half-even rounding to six decimal places. The report does not resample dates or fill missing values. [The original operator guide](stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/fred/BRIEFINGS.md) explains every calculation state and baseline rule.

## Continue in the original FRED application

Use your existing Stellar Forge installation containing the analyst briefing feature and its original dependencies. The [maintained installation guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/8f1d879cb1ba2947a05af770091568720ce31f65/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/README.md) describes that installation. Do not run the files in this example as a replacement toolkit.

The following original commands create a **new private example project**. Replace the absolute paths first. Keep the exported package immutable; place the project and generated delivery in separate private directories. Import uses the retained source capture and needs no FRED API key.

```sh
FRED_ROOT=/absolute/extracted-package/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/fred
FRED_PROJECT=/absolute/private/economic-briefing

starforge fred init --project "$FRED_PROJECT" \
  --title "U.S. economic briefing" \
  --selection "$FRED_ROOT/examples/macro-selection.json"

starforge fred import --project "$FRED_PROJECT" \
  --id macro-original --expected-revision 1 \
  --source "$FRED_ROOT/examples/briefing-20261012/macro-source.capture.json"

starforge fred briefing-preview --project "$FRED_PROJECT" \
  --capture 4c7fc88552da69b9448054334bad10b72afee056ed93bcd2fb741d698dde042c \
  --briefing-file "$FRED_ROOT/examples/macro-briefing.json"

starforge fred review --project "$FRED_PROJECT" \
  --id macro-briefing-review --expected-revision 2 \
  --capture 4c7fc88552da69b9448054334bad10b72afee056ed93bcd2fb741d698dde042c \
  --note "$FRED_ROOT/examples/briefing-20261012/review-note.txt" \
  --briefing-file "$FRED_ROOT/examples/macro-briefing.json"

starforge fred briefing --project "$FRED_PROJECT" \
  --review af00af636c9397ac146966fed06588ef531594c65bc1ec289eada76b4af97802

starforge fred briefing-file --project "$FRED_PROJECT" \
  --review af00af636c9397ac146966fed06588ef531594c65bc1ec289eada76b4af97802 \
  --format html --out /absolute/delivery/economic-briefing.html
```

The capture ID is `4c7fc88552da69b9448054334bad10b72afee056ed93bcd2fb741d698dde042c`; the unchanged note and selection produce review `af00af636c9397ac146966fed06588ef531594c65bc1ec289eada76b4af97802`. The original native importer verifies the captured source. The report command reads the saved review, and the file command writes its full original HTML.

To continue an existing project, reopen it and read its current revision and retained operation IDs. Do not apply these fresh-project revisions to another project's current state. After an interrupted mutation, inspect/reconcile the same original operation before choosing another ID.

Open the same project's original industrial workspace:

```sh
starforge fred serve --project "$FRED_PROJECT" \
  --connection-file /absolute/private/economic-startup.json
```

In **Editions & review**, open the saved capture/review and its analyst briefing. The existing editor can change the interval, series, exact comparison methods or note and save a new reviewed edition. Keep the original report when saving a changed selection.

Export from the original application once your project contains the reviewed editions you intend to deliver:

```sh
starforge fred export --project "$FRED_PROJECT" \
  --out /absolute/delivery/economic-project.json
starforge fred receive --project /absolute/private/received-economic-project \
  --source /absolute/delivery/economic-project.json
starforge fred serve --project /absolute/private/received-economic-project \
  --connection-file /absolute/private/received-economic-startup.json
```
