# Economic workspace clients and agents

Operate a retained FRED economic product from the installed command, a typed JavaScript client, or the existing authenticated merchant MCP host. All three paths attach to the original economic workspace: the same project, source captures, reviews, publication, merchant listener, configured SF88 buyer and saved customer intents.

The client covers official source intake, complete public-table imports, combined macro editions, observations and revision comparisons, projection review, publication, merchant control, customer preparation/execution/recovery, complete downloads and project receiving. The MCP family contains 30 tools and loads its runtime only when that configured family is used.

## Start or reconnect the original workspace

Use Node 24 and the existing economic application installation. The original workspace owner starts its same project with the configured buyer and facilitator:

~~~sh
starforge fred serve \
  --project /PRIVATE/ORIGINAL_FRED_PROJECT \
  --buyer-config /PRIVATE/ORIGINAL_BUYER.json \
  --facilitator https://ORIGINAL-FACILITATOR \
  --merchant-port ORIGINAL_MERCHANT_PORT \
  --connection-file /PRIVATE/fred-console.json
~~~

The capitalized paths, origin and port select the operator's existing resources. The optional connection-file flag writes the actual startup record with owner-only permissions. It includes the native project ID, complete launch binding and private session URL. On a later start of the same project, the record is replaced atomically; an existing record belonging to another project is rejected. The original managed Application may also supply its retained complete startup record directly.

The workspace binding covers its canonical project directory and creation identity, selected buyer configuration hash/path, facilitator, local-facilitator setting and merchant port. The client reads the native launch endpoint and compares the exact binding before it dispatches a workspace operation. A declared expected binding adds a fixed operator selection. A connection-record rotation reconnects the client to the same project using its current session.

Create the installed client connection using the existing original public payment file:

~~~sh
starforge fred-workspace connection-init \
  --out /PRIVATE/fred-client.json \
  --console-url-file /PRIVATE/fred-console.json \
  --workspace macro \
  --inputs-file stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/examples/fred-workspace-inputs.json \
  --payment-file /PRIVATE/ORIGINAL_PUBLIC_PAYMENT.json \
  --merchant-origin https://ORIGINAL-MERCHANT-HOST \
  --profile native
starforge fred-workspace status --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json
~~~

The connection initializer authenticates an actual launch read before publishing its private connection file. Its returned projectId, bindingSha256 and instanceId identify that original server. Use an existing profiles JSON file with --profiles-file when there are several merchant configurations.

For a complete source checkout the supplied input-alias example resolves directly to the retained UNRATE, CPIAUCSL and GDP source files. Within an installed distribution these same files sit under its source directory. Input aliases are resolved from the input-alias file's directory. Client configuration paths are resolved from the connection file's directory.

The connection schema is stellar-forge.fred-workspace-connection.v1. Each workspace has one consoleUrlFile or consoleUrlEnv reference, optional projectId and expectedBindingSha256, request capacity/time settings, inputs, and merchantProfiles. The file or environment variable retains the original startup JSON or unchanged private URL. A bare URL requires the explicit original projectId. Credential values stay in the original private workspace and buyer configuration.

## Build and review a real macro edition

Read status and inputs first. input-inspect reads the complete selected source file, returning its file SHA256, original publisher-table URL, retrieval time, series ID and original table byte/hash metadata. The configured input digest, when present, is checked again during import.

~~~sh
starforge fred-workspace inputs --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json
starforge fred-workspace input-inspect --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json --input unrate
starforge fred-workspace import --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json \
  --input unrate --id ORIGINAL_IMPORT_ID --revision CURRENT_REVISION --sha256 ORIGINAL_FILE_SHA256
~~~

Continue with the revision and captureId returned by each original operation. Import the declared CPI and GDP files in the same way, then combine their retained capture IDs:

~~~sh
starforge fred-workspace combine --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json \
  --id ORIGINAL_COMBINE_ID --revision CURRENT_REVISION --captures UNRATE_SHA,CPI_SHA,GDP_SHA
starforge fred-workspace observations --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json \
  --capture COMBINED_CAPTURE_SHA --series UNRATE --offset 0
starforge fred-workspace review --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json \
  --id ORIGINAL_REVIEW_ID --revision CURRENT_REVISION --capture COMBINED_CAPTURE_SHA \
  --policy-file ORIGINAL_PROJECTION.json --note-file ORIGINAL_REVIEW.txt
starforge fred-workspace publish --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json \
  --id ORIGINAL_PUBLICATION_ID --revision CURRENT_REVISION --review SAVED_REVIEW_SHA --profile native
~~~

These uppercase IDs/hashes/revisions select values from the actual original operation. Project changes retain their stable id and expectedRevision in the native project journal. An exact repeated completed request returns its saved result. A pending source acquisition continues with its same original ID and revision.

Public-table imports carry the complete original publisher text and supplied retrieval metadata through the maintained parser. Each series retains its frequency, units, seasonal adjustment, publisher and missing values. Public-table retrieval time is represented by the original PUBLIC_TABLE_RETRIEVAL_DATE basis. The FRED API acquisition path retains its original real-time/vintage response fields. The combined product keeps these distinctions in its rows, metadata, source file and saved projection.

The supplied source files contain the actual original full UNRATE, CPIAUCSL and GDP public tables. Their original periods and publisher metadata remain available in each retained source. The macro starter guide describes these inputs in detail: [original macro starter](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/fred/sources/MACRO_STARTER.md).

For official API acquisition, configure saves the actual FRED selection and capture uses the environment-variable reference already recorded in the original project:

~~~sh

  --id ORIGINAL_CONFIGURATION_ID --revision CURRENT_REVISION --selection-file ORIGINAL_SELECTION.json
starforge fred-workspace capture --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json \
~~~

The source model and importer are documented in the [economic application guide](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/fred/README.md). The native edition retains the FRED attribution and [FRED API terms link](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/terms_of_use.html). Official observation parameter semantics are available in the [FRED observations documentation](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/series_observations.html); the client forwards the original workspace selection to that maintained source engine.

## Work with large collections and revisions

records pages captures, reviews, publications and original operations. Retain its returned revision as expectedRevision across that collection. Requests use expectedViewSha256 across their separately changing prepared-intent inventory.

observations and compare use the native 100-row response pages. Follow the returned nextOffset until it is null. A capture ID identifies immutable retained source, so both observation paging and before/after comparisons stay tied to their exact source editions.

~~~sh
starforge fred-workspace records --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json \
  --kind captures --offset 0 --limit 25 --revision CURRENT_REVISION
starforge fred-workspace compare --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json \
  --before EARLIER_CAPTURE_SHA --after LATER_CAPTURE_SHA --offset 0
starforge fred-workspace download --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json \
  --kind comparison --before EARLIER_CAPTURE_SHA --after LATER_CAPTURE_SHA --out /PRIVATE/revisions.json
~~~

The complete comparison download includes every original change. file downloads also retain complete source, project and customer responses.

## Original merchant and customer execution

Read publication to inspect its original snapshot, schema, offers, advertised file paths and complete file hashes. merchant-start forwards that reviewed publication to the original workspace's configured native seller/facilitator.

~~~sh
starforge fred-workspace publication --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json --publication PUBLICATION_SHA
starforge fred-workspace merchant-start --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json --publication PUBLICATION_SHA
starforge fred-workspace preview --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json \
  --publication PUBLICATION_SHA --query 'where_series=UNRATE&limit=100'
starforge fred-workspace prepare --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json \
  --publication PUBLICATION_SHA --intent ORIGINAL_INTENT_ID --query 'where_series=UNRATE&limit=100'
starforge fred-workspace buy --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json \
  --publication PUBLICATION_SHA --intent ORIGINAL_INTENT_ID
~~~

Use the original dataset's declared query fields when choosing filters, sort and limits. preview invokes that exact dataset handler. The prepared customer request binds its offer, selected payment alternative, query, publication, snapshot and output policy before execution.

The configured SF88 buyer performs its existing approval and native execution. The agent result includes the original native metadata, delivery byte count/hash and cursor metadata. Download the complete saved response with the same intent:

~~~sh
starforge fred-workspace recover --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json \
  --publication PUBLICATION_SHA --intent ORIGINAL_INTENT_ID
starforge fred-workspace download --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json \
  --kind customer --publication PUBLICATION_SHA --intent ORIGINAL_INTENT_ID --out /PRIVATE/original-page.json
~~~

For the next dataset page, retain the original preceding page metadata, snapshot and returned nextCursor. Supply that actual cursor in the query and the metadata in --previous-file when preparing the next original intent. Each paid page keeps its own original intent. For a whole source or CSV file, pass the exact path advertised by publication in --file and use the same prepare, buy, recover and complete-download flow.

Every client mutation has one native HTTP request. A lost response retains an ambiguous outcome on the thrown error together with the original ID. Inspect operation for project work and recover the same intent for customer work. A request timeout or client disconnect leaves the original server's operation with its owner. The wait command observes durable project progress through reads; it never dispatches a mutation.

## Export, receive and reconnect

~~~sh
starforge fred-workspace download --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json \
  --kind source --capture CAPTURE_SHA --out /PRIVATE/original-capture.json
starforge fred-workspace download --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json \
  --kind project --out /PRIVATE/fred-project.json
starforge fred-workspace receive --source /PRIVATE/fred-project.json \
  --project /PRIVATE/RECEIVED_FRED_PROJECT --sha256 COMPLETE_DOWNLOAD_SHA256
~~~

The project download checks the native bundle identity and exact project ID. Receiving invokes the maintained original receiveFredProject implementation to reconstruct the source editions, saved reviews and publications. The original customer's native account/ledger and financial operation records remain under their configured custody, while their complete delivered files are exported through the customer download operation.

Downloads preserve the full response bytes, byte count, content type and SHA256. Publication creates a new destination; an already retained identical file is reused after its complete hash and size are checked. A different destination file is preserved and the command returns the conflict.

Reopen the original project or the received directory through fred serve with its same configuration, then retain its actual connection record. A subsequent status reads that record and verifies the same project binding before operating. disconnect releases only the borrowed client and its owned download reads.

## Typed JavaScript interface

The installed exports include buyer/fred/workspace-client, buyer/fred/workspace-client/operations, merchant/mcp/fred and merchant/mcp/fred/setup. Each has an explicit .d.mts declaration. The following source-checkout example uses the same client:

~~~js
import {
  FredWorkspaceClient, readFredWorkspaceConfiguration, saveFredFile
} from './stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/fred-workspace-client.mjs';

const configured = await readFredWorkspaceConfiguration('/PRIVATE/fred-client.json');
const client = new FredWorkspaceClient(configured.workspaces.macro);
try {
  const state = await client.state();
  const captureId = state.project.selectedCapture;
  let offset = 0;
  do {
    const page = await client.observations({ captureId, series: 'UNRATE', offset });
    // Consume page.rows with their original date, value, missing flag and units.
    offset = page.nextOffset;
  } while (offset !== null);
  const retained = await saveFredFile(client, { kind: 'project' }, '/PRIVATE/project-copy.json');
  console.log({ projectId: retained.projectId, bytes: retained.bytes, sha256: retained.sha256 });
} finally {
  client.close();
}
~~~

The definitions expose the original launch binding, project/revision structures, source and publication inputs, exact file selections, raw Buffer downloads and recoverable error fields. The client accepts an AbortSignal per operation; timeoutMs controls the client observation window up to 30 minutes. Full request capacity is 128 MiB and full response capacity is 256 MiB, matching the original workspace and bundle contracts. The original source model applies its own source limits.

## Source and calculation contract

The calculation uses the original source level values. It keeps every observation's series, date, literal value, missing marker, frequency, units, seasonal adjustment, information date and time basis. It does not resample observations or substitute a missing value.

| Selection | Exact baseline |
| --- | --- |
| Previous period: monthly | Same calendar day, one month earlier |
| Previous period: quarterly | Same calendar day, three months earlier |
| Previous period: semiannual / annual | Same calendar day, six / twelve months earlier |
| Previous period: daily / weekly / biweekly | One / seven / fourteen calendar days earlier |
| Year earlier | Same calendar day twelve months earlier; monthly, quarterly, semiannual or annual series |
| Previous observation | Immediately preceding original observation row, including a missing marker |

Baselines come from the same retained capture and may precede the displayed interval. A missing exact calendar date remains absent; a prior missing observation remains missing. Daily or irregular series can use **previous observation** to request that explicitly. Previous-period calendar comparisons retain holidays and other absent dates as absent baselines.

Absolute change is exact decimal subtraction. For a series whose original unit is **Percent**, this difference is labeled **Percentage points**. Other differences retain the original unit.

Relative percent change is separately selected and uses `100 × (current − baseline) / baseline`. The calculation uses integer decimal arithmetic, then rounds to the selected 0–12 decimal places using half-even rounding. The output retains whether rounding occurred. A zero denominator produces `ZERO_BASE` with no numeric relative result.

The [BLS percent-change guide](https://www.bls.gov/cpi/factsheets/calculating-percent-changes.htm) explains the same two-observation formula, matching months for twelve-month changes, and consistent index bases. The original [FRED observations API](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/series_observations.html) provides the source values and real-time fields used by API captures. Public table imports retain their actual table retrieval dates.

CPIAUCSL is an index series. Its absolute difference is in its original index units; its relative change is a percentage. GDP in the starter is nominal quarterly GDP in billions of dollars at a seasonally adjusted annual rate. The report keeps those original units; a quarter-to-quarter relative comparison is the direct ratio of those two published values. It does not annualize that growth rate or convert nominal values to real values.

| Measure state | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `READY` | Both original observations have supported numeric values |
| `SOURCE_MISSING` | The selected current observation has its original missing marker |
| `BASE_ABSENT` | The selected baseline row is outside or absent from the retained source |
| `BASE_MISSING` | The exact baseline has its original missing marker |
| `CALENDAR_DATE_ABSENT` | The selected earlier calendar date does not exist |
| `NUMERIC_LITERAL_UNSUPPORTED` | The original value cannot be interpreted by the supported decimal grammar |

Relative results additionally report `NOT_SELECTED`, `ZERO_BASE` or `SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`. The complete CSV includes both the absolute and relative states.

A briefing selects 1–50 original series and 1–10,000 original observations. The complete source capture remains retained even when the reporting window selects fewer rows. A single native asset is limited to 16 MiB and the publication's combined asset budget is 64 MiB. All four briefing files must fit; the application gives a capacity error before advertising an incomplete report.

Existing `file`/`saveFredFile` accept `{kind:'briefing', reviewId, format:'html'|'csv'|'json'|'manifest'}`. A download first reads the saved original file descriptor, then requires the complete response to match its size and SHA256.

The FRED agent family now contains 30 tools. `merchant_fred_briefing_preview` returns original comparison pages. `merchant_fred_review` saves the optional selection. `merchant_fred_briefing` returns the saved report page and all four file descriptors. `merchant_fred_file_read` with kind `briefing` transfers the complete selected file through the maintained retained-read ID/chunk interface. The existing publication, payment, customer recovery and project export tools continue the same operation.

The pure calculation model and declarations are also exported as `./merchant/fred/briefing`. They accept the complete original FRED model and a source selection; all file/network/payment operations remain in the existing operator surfaces.

## Complete project handover

```sh
starforge fred export --project "$FRED_PROJECT" --out /absolute/delivery/economic-project.json
starforge fred receive --project /absolute/private/received-economic-project \
  --source /absolute/delivery/economic-project.json
starforge fred serve --project /absolute/private/received-economic-project \
  --connection-file /absolute/private/received-economic-startup.json
```

Source-only reviews, editions and project exports preserve their existing v1 identities. A saved analyst review adds its normalized selection to the original review identity. Analyst editions use `stellar-forge.fred-edition.v2`; project bundles containing briefings use `stellar-forge.fred-project-bundle.v2`.

The v2 bundle includes all original source captures and the complete four-file transfer for every analyst review, including unpublished reviews. Receiving validates the source, saved selection, exact calculation model, every file byte/hash and original native publication identity. It preserves the received HTML and CSV bytes. Reopening reads that retained package.

Briefing files are written through private temporary files, synced, linked into create-only destinations, then completed with the manifest last. Resuming the same original review finishes the same files; any differing existing bytes produce a conflict. Source and payment ownership remain with the original configured project and native buyer.

## Attribution

Every report carries the original source metadata and the application's FRED notice and [Terms of Use](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/terms_of_use.html). Preserve the original publisher attribution and applicable source notices when distributing an edition. A saved report identifies its source capture, review, calculation version and full file manifest.

## Responsive rendering revision

The HTML member now uses FRED_OFFLINE_REPORT_V2. Its filter controls fit phone widths and its labelled comparison region supports keyboard scrolling. The original report JSON, measures CSV, capture, review, calculation and report identity are unchanged. Retained V1 files remain readable and exportable.

This source package adds complete CPI and GDP histories to the existing unemployment edition. The maintained FRED application imports the original tables, combines selected retained captures into one economic edition, saves its review, publishes the edition through the original merchant, and receives its data with the original customer.

## Import the three series into one project

Run these commands from the installed source directory `stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/fred`. Keep the private project outside the installed package. The [macro selection](../examples/macro-selection.json) also supplies the original three series and full interval for a subsequent API acquisition using the host's configured FRED key.

```sh
node cli.mjs init --project /absolute/private/macro-project \
  --title "US macroeconomic editions" --selection examples/macro-selection.json
node cli.mjs import --project /absolute/private/macro-project \
  --id macro-cpi-source-20261012 --expected-revision 1 \
  --source sources/cpiaucsl-20261012.public-table.json
node cli.mjs import --project /absolute/private/macro-project \
  --id macro-gdp-source-20261012 --expected-revision 2 \
  --source sources/gdp-20261012.public-table.json
node cli.mjs import --project /absolute/private/macro-project \
  --id macro-unrate-source-20261012 --expected-revision 3 \
  --source sources/unrate-20261012.public-table.json
node cli.mjs serve --project /absolute/private/macro-project --port 0
```

A new project finishes these imports at revision 4 with three retained capture IDs. Each import reports its original capture ID and current revision. When using an existing project, read its current revision with `node cli.mjs show --project /absolute/private/macro-project` and use the actual revision for the next operation.

Open **Editions & review → Combine retained public tables**. Select the CPIAUCSL, GDP and UNRATE captures and choose **Create combined edition**. The resulting capture contains all 2,219 original observations under one retained source identity. Inspect it and save its review.

The same operation is available through the CLI. Use the three capture IDs returned by the original imports:

```sh
node cli.mjs combine --project /absolute/private/macro-project \
  --id macro-combined-20261012 --expected-revision 4 \
  --captures CPI_CAPTURE_SHA,GDP_CAPTURE_SHA,UNRATE_CAPTURE_SHA
```

The command returns the combined capture ID and revision 5. Subsequent reviews and publications use that current revision. When continuing an existing project, use its actual revision and saved operation IDs. You can also review and publish any of the original single-series captures independently. **Merchant** publishes a reviewed edition with the host's existing payment terms and facilitator. **Customer** prepares the exact published request and receives the original paid response. The [application guide](../README.md#publish-and-operate-the-merchant) covers merchant lifetime, native purchase, recovery, pagination and complete project receiving.

## Meaning of this starter

Public-table editions retain the UTC retrieval date in `as_of` and `PUBLIC_TABLE_RETRIEVAL_DATE` in `time_basis`. FRED API captures use the selected real-time period and `FRED_REALTIME_DATE`. Both modes preserve their own source metadata in the retained capture and published manifest.

This starter preserves monthly and quarterly records at their original observation dates. Source values remain their original strings; missing values remain `.` with `missing: true`. Any later calculation of inflation, growth or a common-frequency panel needs an explicit transformation with its own stated method and retained input edition.

To refresh, retain a new complete public-table wrapper or acquire the selected API vintage in the same application. Save a new capture and review. Compare successive captures with the same series and source mode to inspect original added dates, revised values and metadata changes. Exporting the project carries the original captures, reviews, edition plans and operation history together.

## Project and requested outcome

TokenJunkieLabs is building open-source, self-hostable software for a merchant to sell a useful API, dataset or agent operation on Stellar and for its buyer to receive the complete result in an existing application. A purchase connects the approved request, native transfer, usable output and merchant fulfillment. That connection survives interrupted delivery, a changed source edition and handover to another maintainer.

We request **$38,000 for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from award acceptance**. The funded outcome is **two independently operated merchant services and two independent buyer operators**: installed services by day 30, recurring testnet use by day 90, and both merchants operating maintainable mainnet services by day 150. T2 runs the same useful service through two independently operated testnet facilitators.

The working product supplies the architecture and completed development foundation. The award funds the remaining source and receiving adaptations, Stellar deployment, monitoring and recovery improvements needed by the selected independent services. Those reusable improvements return to the public product.

## Customer problem, need and adoption

Our first customer is a recurring API/data-service operator or the agency implementing that service in a customer's application. The commissioning payer buys installation and handover; the independent buyer pays for the useful resource. These roles may belong to different organizations.

For an analyst, completion requires the entire agreed population, original units and time basis, and a usable report. An agent application needs its approved result within the aggregate task budget. A paid page, signed transfer or finished background job is one part of that customer task. The merchant needs to connect accepted output to its offer, fulfillment and accounting.

Two supported installation patterns make the adoption plan concrete:

|Installation pattern|Useful recurring purchase|Customer acceptance|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|A merchant publishes a reviewed economic or operational report.|The buyer acquires the agreed new reporting period or source edition and compares it with the prior result.|Complete report and underlying selected data open in the customer's application, preserving units, periods and source meaning.|
|A merchant sells a typed dataset or saved query.|The buyer acquires a distinct approved query or refreshed population, receiving every agreed paid page and file.|The complete result reopens with its original request, source selection, aggregate cost and merchant records.|


The selection fixes the source, geography or other population, observation period, query and expected customer output before purchase. The merchant reviews the release; the buyer receives the agreed HTML, CSV, JSON or named query result in its analyst workspace. The priced unit is exactly the advertised resource. If a complete task needs several paid pages or separately priced files, the workorder and buyer approval account for their combined cost and full coverage. A new source period or distinct useful query supplies the next purchase.

The two funded installations and agreements remain to be selected. Current conversations clarify the route to them: Veridex invited the existing buyer CLI into its testnet cohort and reported no third-party testing budget; CoCart's founder asked who introduces, pays and contracts for customer work; Blockscout expressed interest and reported no integration budget; Nansen declined. The [detailed customer and commercial plan](./product-and-finance.md#1-customer-problem-and-commercial-model) retains those conversations' scope and proposed workshares.

For each selected installation, the workorder names the payer, merchant, buyer, receiving engineer, authorized source, complete task and output, priced unit, spending limit, host and acceptance owner. The first installed execution establishes the operating baseline. Each following agreed source period, edition or distinct query supplies useful repeat work. The receiving engineer performs an actual change or recovery before handover. That same recurring task continues through the T2 and T3 measurement windows.

A Timescale installation, if selected, applies this scope to original commissioning reports and native source populations, reviewed field/time/quality meanings, baseline-to-observed reconciliation and complete analytical receiving. An aid-data installation connects the original organisation publication and selected activity portfolios to the reviewed financial result, with original document links, captured evidence, named source review and complete analyst receiving. Their complete existing chapters supply the source and receiving architecture; the selected customer workorder determines the actual remaining adaptation and commercial responsibilities.

**The purchase target follows the two selected buyers’ work.** Two buyers making one purchase on each ordinary weekday generate twenty purchases in fourteen consecutive days. Their selected T3 workorders must establish actual demand for at least thirty distinct useful paid requests across those same two buyers and both merchants within the fourteen-day window. Each workorder defines the paid unit before purchase and retains its association with the complete customer task: two paid pages may finish one task, while the task total remains one. Reopening a saved result, retrying its original request and cached use preserve that original purchase and task. Work from another buyer can be evaluated in its own cohort.

## Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar provides native authorization and settlement for the reviewed purchase. In its [x402 Exact flow](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/agentic-payments/x402/built-on-stellar), the buyer signs a Soroban token-transfer authorization binding payer, recipient, atomic amount and expiration. A facilitator submits it on the selected network; fee sponsorship can cover the transaction fee. Our implementation uses existing SDKs and token contracts.

The application retains the endpoint and method or MCP tool and arguments, request identity, selected source, payment option, complete output and fulfillment history. It checks the approved operation before dispatch and joins those application records to the original native transaction. Wallet authority and aggregate spending remain with the buyer; source, pricing and fulfillment authority remain with the merchant.

Stellar's own [x402 CLI guide](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/agent-cli/guides/pay-for-apis-x402) already covers the challenge, signed retry, returned response and transfer confirmation, and explains why saving the full returned body matters when another request incurs another payment. [x402 facilitators](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/blob/main/docs/core-concepts/facilitator.md) supply verification and settlement; [Bazaar](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/blob/main/docs/extensions/bazaar.mdx) supplies discoverable resource schemas. We reuse those foundations and carry the purchased resource through the complete customer task, its aggregate approval, unfinished-result recovery and merchant/accounting handover.

Existing products already provide substantial paid-access capabilities:

|Published foundation|Our funded application contribution|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|[ApiCharge](https://apicharge.com/Documentation/core-concepts.html) deploys typed endpoints and retains purchased route quality of service across pricing changes.|Complete acquired data and reports continue in the customer's editable application and another engineer's installation.|
|[MPP Router](https://www.mpprouter.dev/llms.txt) provides Stellar paid-service discovery, signed asynchronous-job polling and request-ID response caching.|A recurring task retains its exact source/query, all agreed pages and files, original payment, customer output and maintainer recovery.|


Our proposed [Open Track](https://stellar.gitbook.io/scf-handbook/scf-awards/build-award/open-track) contribution is that reusable merchant-to-customer workflow: typed source and receiving interfaces, complete purchase state across independent providers, deployed response and maintainable handover. The six packages implement these capabilities in two independent installations and publish the resulting improvements. Native payments, returning buyers and useful tasks another engineer can continue measure their value to Stellar. The [architecture and ecosystem comparison](./product-and-finance.md#3-why-stellar-and-the-ecosystem-fit) develops the existing-tool comparison.

## Defined architecture and operating behavior

Six connected components carry the customer task:

1. **Merchant workspace.** A private operator selects an authorized source edition or named query, schema, output and limits. Source or terms changes become separately reviewed states.
2. **HTTP or MCP resource.** Source adapters preserve types, nulls, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential references govern source access.
3. **Buyer approval and budget.** The buyer approves the exact method or tool, arguments, source scope and payment option. The original challenge and remote schema must match before signing; per-payment limits and the existing budget reservation govern aggregate spending.
4. **Stellar settlement.** The native signer and facilitator use the reviewed network, asset, recipient, amount, expiry and fee policy. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the resulting transfer. The existing MPP Charge integration retains its own challenge and recovery lifecycle.
5. **Complete delivery and accounting.** The application retains all agreed pages/files, original attempts, accepted output, merchant notification and acknowledgment. A prepaid request keeps its selected pass and consumed allowance when defaults change. Customer pricing retains quantity, period, tariff and supplier-cost basis beside its invoice or service records.
6. **Recovery and receiving.** Confirmation, transfer, output and fulfillment keep separate states. An uncertain response is reconciled through its original dispatch. Another engineer restores configuration, history and customer files, supplies authorized secret references and continues the original work.

**Catalog-to-request continuity.** The buyer service retains each complete original catalog page; the desk and typed clients carry its selected row and payment alternative through review. Browse and search continuations retain the operator's filters and the provider's coverage information. Declared HTTP path and query fields, or MCP tool arguments, guide explicit input. A path template becomes a concrete URL under the configured merchant route; fixed advertised values stay fixed. The native HTTP workflow then retains that exact request, body and spending limit in its original durable intent. Operators select the same service workspace when they reopen its status, recovery and saved output. Complete response downloads verify the retained byte count and hash. These capabilities are delivered in the [buyer discovery and native request package](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/689).

**Close recurring service.** A merchant connects each prepaid service order to its customer, retains usage captures, and chooses the opening and closing records for the period. The customer workbench carries those records through reviewed statements, saved closing cycles, corrections and complete customer handovers. Purchase amounts, service activity and separately issued invoices remain available in their own financial records.

Node.js implements the browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces; source and receiving applications also use Python/SQLite and PHP/WordPress/WooCommerce. The defined scope builds on existing Stellar SDKs and contracts. Each deployed facilitator has explicit network, asset, recipient, signing-account and fee policies. T2 configures the same service for two compatible testnet operators; T3 deploys each merchant's reviewed mainnet configuration. The [native signer and facilitator guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/68929767fd9c138e3bcee2df65ea9e5928ca565a/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/native-facilitator/README.md) describes that operating foundation.

## Threat response and outcome measurement
The T2 response package includes a documented threat model, its corresponding installed monitoring plan, and material corrections. Each installation records its source edition, authority, network, facilitator, protected records, observations, thresholds, notification destinations and primary/backup responders. Threats include changed offers or approvals, wrong payment/output attribution, unauthorized access, interrupted delivery, missing observations and restoration of the wrong generation. Each threat is linked to an observable signal, a monitor, an accountable responder and the recovery action; source and delivery failures receive the appropriate application-level observation. The plan follows Stellar's [threat-modeling guidance](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/security-docs/threat-modeling) and [builder monitoring template](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/security-docs/monitoring/monitoring-template-builders).

The customer operates an interrupted settled purchase and a merchant-delivery failure, retaining financial and delivery states, notification and acknowledgment, response/recovery times and useful output. The receiving engineer reopens the original incident after restart; observation gaps remain visible.

A completed purchase requires one distinct approved intent, independently observed native transfer and complete useful output. Transactions are deduplicated per network, with assets and fees recorded separately. A prepaid pass counts once after its first agreed operation produces complete accepted output; later calls are usage. A customer task completes when every agreed page, file and required order action is accepted. Thus the HPD acquisition is two purchases and one complete task.

T2 requires **10 purchases in total across two independent buyers during seven consecutive days ending by day 90**. T3 requires **30 in total during fourteen consecutive days ending by day 150**, with both buyers returning on another UTC day for a distinct completed purchase. Both merchants receive independent use. Independence refers to the accountable organization/person across agents and wallets.

Each cohort retains attempted, completed, partial, unresolved, canceled and refunded outcomes. The original first attempt determines window membership; settlement and complete accepted output must occur within that window. Later observations retain their actual timing. The two-facilitator comparison uses the same service, schema, population and output.

Customer benefit compares the prior task, first installed execution and recurring use on the same population or period: active effort, manual corrections, time to accepted output and unresolved work. For a stated period, calculate direct labor value from completed tasks, comparable active hours saved and the customer's stated hourly value; subtract implementation and incremental provider, hosting, payment and support costs. The original workorder retains those inputs alongside accepted milestones, fees, collections and support effort.

## Build application · SCF #46 · Open Track

**TokenJunkieLabs requests USD 38,000 equivalent in XLM for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance.** The work installs a useful paid Stellar service with two independently operated merchants, two independent buyer operators and the same selected operation through two independently operated facilitators.

## 1. Customer problem and commercial model

An API or data-service operator needs to expose a useful resource to agent applications while retaining access rules, source meaning and commercial control. A buyer needs the complete result it approved and a way to resolve an interrupted paid request. The difficult join spans four records: approved request, settled transfer, delivered output and accepted fulfillment or accounting.

Current x402 reports show the practical need for that join. One October 2 report described payment-bearing requests rejected because a merchant required POST while the reference client retried GET; health and catalogue checks had appeared normal. The author subsequently corrected the server. An October 3 report described settlement without a discovery listing; a separate operator later reported successful indexing of its own resources and explained the facilitator diagnostics in that thread. These were Base deployments. They show how a healthy catalogue or settled payment can leave the customer's task unfinished. Our Stellar implementation retains the exact request and each original outcome so the unfinished step can be recovered. [Method report](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/issues/3657) · [Discovery report](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/issues/3677)

We serve recurring API/data-service operators, the developers using their results and agencies commissioned to integrate them. A fixed-fee implementation delivers one agreed operation and a handover the receiving engineer can maintain. Further care has its own scope. The commissioning payer, merchant controlling the resource and independent buyer may be different organizations. The workorder names each role, its source and host authority, payment responsibility and acceptance owner. The merchant retains its API or product receipts; TokenJunkieLabs invoices the implementation.

The selected customer task and the priced unit are recorded together. A complete report may require several paid pages. A handover may contain many files or transport chunks. The buyer retains per-request and aggregate spending controls while the operating record shows whether the whole task is complete. A later reporting period, changed source edition, fresh query or new order gives the same buyer a reason to use the service again.

## 2. Product architecture and control

Six connected components form the application: the merchant's private source/release workspace; its HTTP or MCP operation; the native Stellar SDK and configured facilitator; the buyer's private approval and spending state; complete result and delivery records; and merchant fulfillment/accounting. Merchant and buyer services run on their operators' hosts. Approved operations are public; administration, provider credentials, signer references and operating state stay private.

| Stage | Implemented customer control |
| --- | --- |
| Review and publish | Review a source edition or named live query, its arguments and schema, public fields, output limits and complete payment alternatives. Save rights, route, network, asset, recipient, atomic amount and authorization lifetime. Changes or withdrawal become new reviewed states. |
| Connect the source | Preserve original types, missing/null values, pagination and snapshot/live meaning. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth aliases select access and the existing quota/cache state. Retain the edition behind each result. |
| Approve and purchase | Save the actual endpoint, method or tool, arguments, payment option and result scope. Match remote schema and challenge to that selection before signing. Keep the per-payment ceiling and the application's aggregate reservation/budget owner. |
| Settle and deliver | Use the configured native SDK/facilitator for verification and settlement. Save the server's response, full output, byte identity and durable merchant notification. Independently reconcile transaction network, asset, payer, payee and atomic amount. |
| Use and maintain | Receive every selected page or file into the customer's existing application, query, report or workbook. Preserve the parent acquisition and earlier source editions. Existing order and finance authorities control fulfillment, refunds and accounting. |
| Deploy and receive | Select the release, HTTPS service, restricted administration and supervision. Drain, restart, roll back and restore with the original configuration, history and complete customer files. |

The native x402 flow reuses the existing Exact Stellar scheme, token contracts and facilitator supported/verification/settlement interfaces. For paid MCP, the HTTP endpoint, tool and arguments remain distinct from the payment resource. An unsigned call obtains the challenge; the full payment option must match the saved quote before the signed call is dispatched. The official MCP SDK transports the payment and settlement metadata.

Server confirmation, independently observed transfer, complete useful output, receiver acknowledgment and order fulfillment remain separately visible. An uncertain signed reply retains its dispatch state for reconciliation. Reopening a consumed quote returns saved work. Recovery of a complete retained result uses that saved result. A new request or changed purchase gets its own review. Complete export and restore carry the configuration, history and referenced files; the receiving host supplies current authorized secret references.

Browser, CLI, MCP and installed Applications use these same saved workspaces. Native source registrations connect setup, operation and lifecycle while preserving each source adapter's data semantics. The existing request-collection, buyer-to-Operations and document-analysis extensions retain their own original recovery operations; their pending native receiving stages are reported separately from the completed examples below.

## 3. Why Stellar and the ecosystem fit

Stellar settles the approved operation. Buyer approval binds the complete request to its network, asset, recipient and integer atomic amount. Existing libraries and payment services sign, verify and settle; our application connects the transfer to complete output and practical merchant fulfillment.

| Existing component | What it supplies | What this product contributes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native Stellar x402 and OpenZeppelin facilitator | Supported payment options, buyer-authorization verification and settlement | The approved HTTP/MCP request, original source, complete output and recoverable receiving operation |
| Vellar discovery | Optional discovery extension and best-effort catalogue updates independent of settlement | Saved offer/schema/terms and a complete source edition that remains usable through customer review and handover |
| Stellar MPP | Charge for individual requests; Session with funded channels and cumulative commitments | An existing Charge workbench that retains the native challenge, request and merchant profile through concurrent preparation and restart |

OpenZeppelin, Vellar, Veridex and Periplo remain payment-infrastructure choices. Rumble Fish is developing facilitator, discovery and SDK capabilities. We build on those components and return reusable integration and receiving improvements to the public source.

A retained comparison found 27 Vellar offers and two Periplo offers with no shared seller/route identity. The funded two-facilitator deployment therefore includes registering and integrating the same useful operation with both. Each completion will retain the selected provider's actual scheme, network, asset and fee policy. This makes the cost and effort of changing payment infrastructure observable while the merchant service and buyer task remain defined.

A data team operating RisingWave can commission a complete customer-delivery service around an existing table or materialized view. ## Service recovery that reaches the buyer’s books

### The customer outcome

A buyer needs the useful service it purchased and a correct record of what happened when delivery failed. The merchant may recover the output, agree a partial return or identify a remaining correction. The buyer then needs the credit to reach the right expense item, reporting period and accountant handoff. Keeping those links saves staff from repeatedly matching support tickets, payment records, exported files and bookkeeping rows.

The Service-to-buyer operation carries that work through one saved customer case. The merchant selects its Service report and explicit monetary basis. Its configured accounting operator reviews the adjustment and the returned-transfer evidence. ## Customer value and delivery economics

Evaluate the complete task and its recurrence. Let F be the one-time implementation fee, V the customer’s stated value of an hour, H the measured active hours saved per equivalent completed task, N the number of useful repeat tasks, and C the period’s incremental provider, hosting, payment and support cost. The direct labor-value comparison is `N × H × V − F − C`; the effort reduction per task needed to recover the fee is `(F + C) / (N × V)`.

The following planning example assumes twelve monthly tasks and zero entered incremental costs. The two hourly values are explicit scenarios for the customer to replace with its own value; the prior and installed tasks must retain comparable source scope and usable output.

|Implementation fee|Assumed customer hour value|Hours recovered across twelve tasks|Hours per monthly task|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|$3,600|$75|48.00|4.00|
|$3,600|$125|28.80|2.40|
|$4,800|$75|64.00|5.33|
|$4,800|$125|38.40|3.20|
|$7,200|$75|96.00|8.00|
|$7,200|$125|57.60|4.80|


Enter actual incremental costs before using the comparison for an accepted engagement. At a $4,800 fee and $125/hour value, the year needs 38.4 avoided hours plus another avoided hour for each $125 of incremental cost. Reducing a four-hour monthly task to one hour yields 36 hours a year, so that scenario requires further useful value or a different fee/scope to recover the implementation fee in the first year.

|Remaining difference before incremental cost|$7,200 − $5,700 − $360|$1,140|

TokenJunkieLabs requests USD 38,000 equivalent in XLM for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance. The work installs a useful paid Stellar service with two independently operated merchants, two independent buyer operators and the same selected operation through two independently operated facilitators.

The product is open-source, self-hostable merchant and buyer tooling. It carries an approved API request, dataset or paid MCP tool through native settlement, complete useful output, fulfillment and operating handover. The merchant controls its source and terms. The buyer controls its keys, request and spending. Another engineer can reopen the installation and recover unfinished work.

The working development baseline comprises 18 distinct team-operated purchases totaling 411,000 stroops, or 0.0411 native testnet XLM, with network fees recorded separately. The funded milestones establish independent customer operation, repeated use and production receiving from that baseline.

Project and requested outcome

TokenJunkieLabs is building open-source, self-hostable software for a merchant to sell a useful API, dataset or agent operation on Stellar and for its buyer to receive the complete result in an existing application. A purchase connects the approved request, native transfer, usable output and merchant fulfillment. That connection survives interrupted delivery, a changed source edition and handover to another maintainer.

We request $38,000 for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from award acceptance. The funded outcome is two independently operated merchant services and two independent buyer operators: installed services by day 30, recurring testnet use by day 90, and both merchants operating maintainable mainnet services by day 150. T2 runs the same useful service through two independently operated testnet facilitators.

The working product supplies the architecture and completed development foundation. The award funds the remaining source and receiving adaptations, Stellar deployment, monitoring and recovery improvements needed by the selected independent services. Those reusable improvements return to the public product.

Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar provides native authorization and settlement for the reviewed purchase. In its x402 Exact flow, the buyer signs a Soroban token-transfer authorization binding payer, recipient, atomic amount and expiration. A facilitator submits it on the selected network; fee sponsorship can cover the transaction fee. Our implementation uses existing SDKs and token contracts.

Defined architecture and operating behavior

Six connected components carry the customer task:

  1. Merchant workspace. A private operator selects an authorized source edition or named query, schema, output and limits. Source or terms changes become separately reviewed states.
  2. HTTP or MCP resource. Source adapters preserve types, nulls, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential references govern source access.
  3. Buyer approval and budget. The buyer approves the exact method or tool, arguments, source scope and payment option. The original challenge and remote schema must match before signing; per-payment limits and the existing budget reservation govern aggregate spending.
  4. Stellar settlement. The native signer and facilitator use the reviewed network, asset, recipient, amount, expiry and fee policy. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the resulting transfer. The existing MPP Charge integration retains its own challenge and recovery lifecycle.
  5. Complete delivery and accounting. The application retains all agreed pages/files, original attempts, accepted output, merchant notification and acknowledgment. A prepaid request keeps its selected pass and consumed allowance when defaults change. Customer pricing retains quantity, period, tariff and supplier-cost basis beside its invoice or service records.
  6. Recovery and receiving. Confirmation, transfer, output and fulfillment keep separate states. An uncertain response is reconciled through its original dispatch. Another engineer restores configuration, history and customer files, supplies authorized secret references and continues the original work.

Catalog-to-request continuity. The buyer service retains each complete original catalog page; the desk and typed clients carry its selected row and payment alternative through review. Browse and search continuations retain the operator's filters and the provider's coverage information. Declared HTTP path and query fields, or MCP tool arguments, guide explicit input. A path template becomes a concrete URL under the configured merchant route; fixed advertised values stay fixed. The native HTTP workflow then retains that exact request, body and spending limit in its original durable intent. Operators select the same service workspace when they reopen its status, recovery and saved output. Complete response downloads verify the retained byte count and hash. These capabilities are delivered in the buyer discovery and native request package.

Close recurring service. A merchant connects each prepaid service order to its customer, retains usage captures, and chooses the opening and closing records for the period. The customer workbench carries those records through reviewed statements, saved closing cycles, corrections and complete customer handovers. Purchase amounts, service activity and separately issued invoices remain available in their own financial records.

Node.js implements the browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces; source and receiving applications also use Python/SQLite and PHP/WordPress/WooCommerce. The defined scope builds on existing Stellar SDKs and contracts. Each deployed facilitator has explicit network, asset, recipient, signing-account and fee policies. T2 configures the same service for two compatible testnet operators; T3 deploys each merchant's reviewed mainnet configuration. The native signer and facilitator guide describes that operating foundation.

Threat response and outcome measurement

The T2 response package includes a documented threat model, its corresponding installed monitoring plan, and material corrections. Each installation records its source edition, authority, network, facilitator, protected records, observations, thresholds, notification destinations and primary/backup responders. Threats include changed offers or approvals, wrong payment/output attribution, unauthorized access, interrupted delivery, missing observations and restoration of the wrong generation. Each threat is linked to an observable signal, a monitor, an accountable responder and the recovery action; source and delivery failures receive the appropriate application-level observation. The plan follows Stellar's threat-modeling guidance and builder monitoring template.

The customer operates an interrupted settled purchase and a merchant-delivery failure, retaining financial and delivery states, notification and acknowledgment, response/recovery times and useful output. The receiving engineer reopens the original incident after restart; observation gaps remain visible.

A completed purchase requires one distinct approved intent, independently observed native transfer and complete useful output. Transactions are deduplicated per network, with assets and fees recorded separately. A prepaid pass counts once after its first agreed operation produces complete accepted output; later calls are usage. A customer task completes when every agreed page, file and required order action is accepted. Thus the HPD acquisition is two purchases and one complete task.

T2 requires 10 purchases in total across two independent buyers during seven consecutive days ending by day 90. T3 requires 30 in total during fourteen consecutive days ending by day 150, with both buyers returning on another UTC day for a distinct completed purchase. Both merchants receive independent use. Independence refers to the accountable organization/person across agents and wallets.

Each cohort retains attempted, completed, partial, unresolved, canceled and refunded outcomes. The original first attempt determines window membership; settlement and complete accepted output must occur within that window. Later observations retain their actual timing. The two-facilitator comparison uses the same service, schema, population and output.

Customer benefit compares the prior task, first installed execution and recurring use on the same population or period: active effort, manual corrections, time to accepted output and unresolved work. For a stated period, calculate direct labor value from completed tasks, comparable active hours saved and the customer's stated hourly value; subtract implementation and incremental provider, hosting, payment and support costs. The original workorder retains those inputs alongside accepted milestones, fees, collections and support effort.
